=== PAGE: https://www.skydivecoastalcarolinas.com/blog/an-island-tour-from-13000-feet/
TITLE: An Island Tour from 13,000 Feet - Skydiving in North Carolina: An Island Tour from 13,000 Feet
Wanna know a secret? Come a little closer and we’ll tell you.
Here it is: Skydiving is the original Gilligan’s Island.
Confused? Here’s what we’re getting at: Lots of people go for a tandem skydive–the “three-hour tour” of legend–and never really return to life as they knew it before. The experience is so delightful–so inspiring–so paradigm-shifting–that they run right back to the manifest desk to book another jump, and another, and another, and before they know it, they’ve got their solo licenses and they’re spending every spare minute in the sky.
If that seems pretty far-fetched to you, no worries. It did to us, too, before it happened. The folks you see working and playing at Skydive Coastal Carolinas are happy shipmates on a boat that never returned to its original port, and we couldn’t be more stoked about that.
It’ll make more sense once you know a little bit about the ports of call that we visit while we’re up in the wild blue yonder, perhaps, so we’ll share: here’s a quick island tour of the stunnin’ Southport area, as seen from 13,000 feet in the sky. If Southport and Oak Island are an annual vacation destination for you, you probably think you’ve done and seen it all–but here’s a different perspective.
THE ATLANTIC
Looking out at the ocean from ground level is such an iconic vacation experience that nobody visiting Southport would dream of missing it. Right? Well, believe us when we tell you that looking out over its blue expanse from 13,000 feet is a whole new ball game. You get the same feeling of bubbly awe as you do when you’re looking up into the stars from the middle of the desert–a giddy sense of your own smallness, coupled to a deep sense of peace. We never get tired of the feeling.
Here’s a pro tip, too: If you want the extra-strength experience, go for a sunset jump. Sunset jumps are a skydiving classic for stone-cold pros and first-time tandem students alike, and for excellent reason: A sunset jump is one of the most profoundly beautiful experiences a human being can have. If you don’t believe us, try it–and see what it’s like to see the planet drenched in golden honey, saying nighty-night to the sun from an eye-to-eye perspective. Ain’t nothin’ like it.
BALD HEAD ISLAND
The quaint perfection of Bald Head Island is so remote that you can only get there via ferry–and it’s only navigable in a golf cart. In fact, more sea turtles than people call Bald Head Island home by a factor of several thousand. This lovely little rock served numerous eyebrow-raising masters in its post-Native-American history (the British, during the war for independence, and the Confederates in the Civil War); the long peacetime has seen it morph into a popular weekending spot for folks who like the sense of cozy solitude.
From altitude, we love to gaze upon Bald Head’s shimmering network of wetlands, the white ribbon of its undulating coastline and the very-historic lighthouse that’s meant to keep unsuspecting eggs off the Frying Pan Shoals.
OAK ISLAND LIGHTHOUSE
Oak Island Lighthouse has been a local icon since anyone can remember. It juts its proud candy-cane tower up over Caswell’s white sands, keeping watch over a brood of charming little cabins and sunbathers. We love the fact that Oak Island Lighthouse has an architectural “secret” that you can’t see from the outside: instead of a spiral staircase that swoops around the inner tower, Oak Island sports seven ladders that zigzag up to its top. (We can only imagine the workout that early lighthouse-keepers must have had–colonial Crossfit, for sure.)
From altitude, Oak Island serves as something of a sundial. Over the course of a day’s jumps, we watch her slowly draw an arc across the landscape. It’s kinda like she’s waving at us.
THE SOUTHPORT PIER
Ah, our beloved Southport Pier. We spend our evenings scooting around Southport’s bustling little center (and taking on long, heart-pumping runs down the Riverwalk trail to burn off the yummy goodies for which Southport is so famous). We love it best, though, from up above.
The rippling terrain around the Pier–the yacht basin; the peninsula; the boardwalks; the lacy network of waterways–has long been marked as a site of interest on the NC Birding Trail, and you can occasionally see the glinting binoculars as the birdwatchers notice our parachutes in their perusals of the sky. Then, of course, there’s the beach–and the miniature figures of swimsuited merrymakers sunning and playing as we fly. When they wave up at us, we return the favor–and hope they’ll trade their swimsuit for a jumpsuit soon, ’cause they just don’t know what they’re missing.
We’ve got a “three-hour tour” they’re gonna fall head over heels in love with, after all. ;)

Join the ultimate 21+ Happy Hour Cruise in Myrtle Beach, SC! Enjoy a 3-hour experience (1.5 hr cruise + 1.5 hr dockside party) with scenic views, great music, and cold drinks aboard our custom-built party boat. Upcoming Special events… Pie-Eyed Parrot is host to many amazing cruises, Holiday Cruise, Dinner Cruise, July 4th Fireworks Cruise and many more. See about all Myrtle Beach Cruises.
A Fun, Relaxing Cruise in
Myrtle Beach, SC
Escape the everyday with Cruise Tours and enjoy a scenic Myrtle Beach happy hour cruise. Perfect for adults looking for a laid-back, enjoyable experience. Our tours offer refreshing drinks, beautiful views, and great company. Whether you're celebrating or simply unwinding, this is the perfect way to spend your afternoon.
Private Events Cruise
Book your next Party with us on the Pie-Eyed Parrot, and make your next event special. Whether it being a wedding party, birthday, anniversary, retirement corporate event, business party or any special day you want to create great memories, this is the cruise for you.
Pie-Eyed Parrot | Murrells Inlet Happy Hour Cruise
Experience the most amazing sunsets like nowhere else in the Grand Strand right here in Murrells Inlet, South Carolina on the “Happy Hour “ boat. The Pie-Eyed Parrot Happy Hour is a newly built 63’ 120 passenger vessel boasting 2 large decks, a covered lower deck which accommodates up to 70 passengers and an upper sky-view deck accommodating 50. Both decks offer open air with no obstructions making every seat a great seat. The State of the art sound system keeps the music pumping, playing upbeat, fun music for dancing or just sitting back with drink in hand enjoying a great night out with family and friends. Perimeter seating and high top tables accommodate small and large groups. Servers keep the drinks flowing offering beer, wine, frozens and signature cocktails and of course some light appetizers for snacking along the way. Not to worry, we do have a bathroom on board as well.
Join us on the Pie-Eyed Parrot Ultimate Happy Hour Sunset Cruise for an excursion you won’t soon forget. Bring along your camera to capture the breathtaking views of the saltwater marsh and all that is living within this magnificent natural habitat. You never know what you may see between the gorgeous sunsets and sealife, but I can guarantee that you will have a fun time! Just remember, this isn’t just a boat ride, it’s an experience on the Pie-Eyed Parrot Happy Hour Cruise that you will not find on any other vessel. This USCG Certified boat “Happy Hour” was designed to do just what we do, happy hour sunset cruises.
Don’t Miss The Boat … Cruises often sell out so buy your tickets early. We are Coast Guard regulated and only permitted to carry a certain number of passengers. Book Now!: As always, you must be 21 years of age or older to board and present a valid ID, no exceptions.

If it is the tenacious smallmouth bass you desire, let us take you on the trip of your life! We provide one of the best smallmouth bass fishing charters on Lake Erie.
We start catching bronze backs in early May however smallmouth bass are active through October. Tube jigs are the bait of choice. Smallmouth Bass Factoids
One might think the Smallmouth bass are not described properly as they have a fairly large mouth. It extends to they eye all the way to their eye. The key factoid is the mouth does not extend beyond the eye, in contrast the largemouth bass’ mouth does extend past the eye. Young smallmouth bass have an orange color in the center of their tail furthermore distinguishing them from other bass. The smallmouth bass is in the Centrachidae (sunfishes) family, and furthermore is also called a bronzeback, brown bass, brownie, smallie, and black bass. Smallmouth bass generally range in length from 12 to 15 inches and weight from 1 to 2 pounds. However, they have been known to reach 24 inches and 10 pounds hence hooking one of these monsters rivals any fight you may have had with other fish.

WALLEYE FISHING CHARTERS
Lake Erie produces many big walleye as a result the enforcers a 15” minimum size limit and 6 per day per person.
Ohio and Lake Erie are have long been know as the furthermore many would say this is the very best area of Lake Erie to find Walleye Fishing Charters

Walleye Capital of the World
Millions of walleye are fished from Lake Erie yearly therefore we start fishing on our 30 boats just after ice out ( mid March ). By starting early we ensure we get our share as well this is considered by many as Trophy Time.
Jiggs (walleye killer Jiggs) tipped with Minnows, blade baits (silver buddy, cicadas, vibies) and slow trolling are the hottest ticket but above all you need to be holding the rod to land your monster walleye!.
We drift off shore over our favorite reefs and spawning beds until early May. We then switch to spinners topped with night crawlers because and as the walleye becoming more active. Our spinners of choice are weapons, Erie dearies, bottom bouncers therefore we carry these on board.
Spinners are the lure of choice when drifting until early November due to the wind potentially dying out and the lake goes flat calm you may want to break out the trolling gear. At this point we will put out the planner boards and jet divers rigged with spoons ( Michigan stingers and Yeck ) or crank baits ( Bandits,Husky Jerks, Smithwick P-10s and P-20s, Reefrunners ).
Walleye Factoids
During the spawn March and April, Trophy Time. Remember if you LIMIT early you can keep fishing to get your full day in. Some walleye have been found to be over twelve years old as a result of fishing limits!
The average walleye caught in Lake Erie is in the 2 to 5 pound range. Walleye over ten pounds are not uncommon. Most people agree that the smaller walleye are the best eating fish, second only to the yellow perch.
Walleye are light sensitive as a result they may not be near the surface on a sunny day therefore they will often be in the top ten feet on cloudy days.
We have two populations of walleye: resident population that live around the reefs and islands in the western basin all year. The other a migrating population that roams East and West throughout the year as a result walleye are considered to be a schooling fish.

Can I reserve a private space?

Can dietary restrictions be accommodated?

What happens if there is bad weather?

Where are you located?

=== PAGE: https://www.al-almas.com/faq/
TITLE: FAQ – al-almas
Frequently Asked Questions
What is included with my ticket price?
Listed prices per guest include cruise, meal, dessert, and sales tax. Beverages are additional and may be pre-purchased at a discounted rate or at regular purchase price during your cruise. Gratuity for onboard staff is not included; please tip your service crew.
Are my purchased public cruise tickets refundable?
In order to reserve your place aboard a public cruise, payment is required in full prior to your cruise at the time of booking. This payment is NON-REFUNDABLE. Boats depart promptly at the scheduled departure time. If you miss the cruise for any reason, we will consider you a no-show and your tickets will be forfeited by our ticketing system; no refunds will be given and reservations may not be rescheduled for no-show reservations.
If my party is not able to make the departure time or we miss our public cruise time, can I receive a refund?
In order to honor all guests, boats leave the dock as scheduled. Please allow plenty of time for parking and plan to arrive at least 15 minutes prior to your cruise departure time to ensure you make it to the boat.
Will my cruise reservation be cancelled?
RARELY! We cruise rain or shine, but we do require 20 adult reservations for departure. It is very rare that we cancel due to lack of participation but in such event, we will provide you with 24 hour notice, and offer you a refund or opportunity to reschedule.
What happens during rain or storms?
Al and Alma’s Fleet cruises rain or shine. In the case of severe weather conditions, the yachts may be held dockside for portions of the event. Also, please keep in mind that our yachts are equipped with full upper deck enclosures to protect you from the weather. No refunds will be issued as a result of weather.
Is smoking permitted?
No. Smoking of any kind is NOT permitted anywhere on Al & Alma’s yachts – this includes both indoor areas and outside decks.
What payment options do I have?
Payments can be made by credit card or Al and Alma’s gift card. One gift card may be redeemed per transaction. We accept Visa, MasterCard, Discover, and American Express. Public cruise tickets can only be purchased online via our website.
Are your yachts Handicap Accessible?
Regrettably, none of the yachts in Al and Alma’s fleet are “Handicap Accessible” as determined by state law. The variable water levels and dual decks on each boat require all of our guests to make a few steps up and down to board the boats. Our crew is very accommodating and will work with you to provide access to our yachts. Please call us for specific details regarding accessibility questions. Please make us aware of any special mobility issues or concerns upon reservations so that our crew is prepared to serve you.
Are your buffets “all you can eat”?
No. Our food is served buffet style, but it is not “all you can eat.” Though we provide generous serving portions, because of the finality of being on the water, our buffet cruises leave the dock with specific portion servings per person. Your host or hostess will work to make sure your guests receive appropriate portion servings.
Are there vegetarian and gluten-free options available?
Absolutely. Please note your dietary request when you book your reservation online, and a special meal will be provided in exchange of the buffet option.
Are children allowed?
Of course! Adults must accompany children. Though not required, we do recommend that small children bring a comfortable life jacket to wear during the cruise. Children three and under cruise for free. Children ten and under cruise at a reduced rate for private cruises.
Are outside alcoholic beverages allowed?
No. Minnesota State Law forbids us from allowing any outside alcoholic beverages onboard Al and Alma’s fleet.
What is the dress attire?
Dress for the current weather conditions during your cruise time. As a general rule, we recommend casual dress attire, such as casual shorts or pants and golf shirts.
Is there pre-assigned seating on public cruises?
Rarely. Cruises open to the public begin boarding 15 minutes prior to departure. Seating choices are on a first come basis. During holidays and some signature events we will assign seating in our best effort to keep groups together.

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

Southern Shores Cruises FAQ
Some Of Our Most Frequently Asked Questions!
Welcome to the Southern Shores Cruises FAQ page! Here, you’ll find answers to common questions about our luxurious coastal cruise experiences. Whether you’re curious about our itineraries, onboard amenities, or how to book your dream getaway, we’ve got you covered. Explore everything Southern Shores Cruises has to offer and get ready to set sail on an unforgettable journey!
Reservations are made from the home page on our website. Please choose the type of cruise and the time you want and pay for the reservation through the Fareharbor booking platform provided.
Please arrive AT LEAST 30 min prior to your scheduled cruise time. The boat will leave the dock promptly at its scheduled time. We will not wait on guests even if you have a reservation.
No outside food or drink is allowed on the boat UNLESS you have booked one of the private charters. The Catamaran dolphin cruise will have drinks, snacks and alcohol for sale during the trip. Drinks and snacks will also be available for purchase at the ticket booth prior to boarding for the jet boat ride. The offshore boating experience includes a cooler onboard that will have complimentary waters and sodas. No coolers are allowed on the boat with the exception of private charters.
The boat leaves from the face dock at Cherry Grove Marina 2201 Little River Neck Rd. North Myrtle Beach, SC 29582
There are designated parking spots just past the marina office on the right side of the road near the ticket booth. Parking is free.
Please bring your friends, family and a good attitude! We will provide all required life jackets and safety equipment. The Thrillseeker is a wet ride, so you may want a change of clothes or a towel for after the ride.
The catamaran and the Need 4 Speed have bathrooms onboard. The Thrillseeker does not. Restrooms are available at the ticket booth for all rides. We recommend all guests use the restroom before boarding the boat.
The catamaran and need 4 speed are suitable for all ages. The Thrillseeker has a minimum height requirement of at least 42 inches to be able to ride.
Safety is the highest priority. We will cancel all cruises if there is inclement weather that makes it too dangerous to go out. If a cruise is cancelled we will notify you by phone if possible. Do not assume a cruise is cancelled because of the weather report! Keep in mind, we are a coastal town and weather is unpredictable and moves in quickly at times. We will do our best to provide ample notification for any cancellations, but if inclement weather is incoming cancellations may take place less than 30 minutes prior to scheduled cruise times. We will reschedule or refund any weather cancellations with no additional fees.
Ocean conditions change rapidly throughout the day and are subject to many variables. Typically the conditions are more favorable earlier in the day, and wave height and wind speed increases in the afternoon. If the Coast Guard issues a small craft advisory we will not take the boat into the Ocean. This does not mean the cruise is cancelled. As an alternative we will spend more time at the beach and/or cruise longer on the ICW into North Carolina.
Cancellations can be made online or by phone with at least 48 hour notice. A cancellation made within the 48-hour window will be issued a gift card for the amount of the purchase to be redeemed at any time with a reservation.
No shows will not be refunded any amount, we will offer a stand by ticket for another trip, and you will be able to go if the boat is not filled

Ocean Explorers marine science summer program at Seymour Center is a week your budding scientist will never forget! Just ask the professional marine scientists who attended Ocean Explorers when they were kids.
Our ocean science summer programs give youth ages 7 to 14 opportunities to actively explore the coast, investigate the fascinating animals of Monterey Bay, and experience the thrill of scientific discovery at a world-class marine lab.
Discover the amazing animals that call our coastline home. In Coastal Creatures, we’ll explore how sea stars cling to rocks, crabs protect themselves with hard shells, seabirds use specialized beaks to find food, and other coastal animals rely on unique body structures to survive. Through aquarium investigations, hands-on activities, and shoreline exploration, participants will observe these adaptations up close and learn how form helps function in the wild. === PAGE: https://seymourcenter.ucsc.edu/about/
TITLE: About – Seymour Marine Discovery Center
About
Community-supported marine science education center operated by the University of California, Santa Cruz.
On This Page
Through our breathtaking seaside learning center, we bring the adventures and explorations of ocean science to life. Powered by the Long Marine Laboratory, a world-renowned university research facility, the Seymour Marine Discovery Center offers hands-on immersion into the world of ocean exploration and discovery. In our 20,000-square-foot visitor center, guests can touch a shark, explore the latest discoveries in ocean science, and take in the spectacular Monterey Bay, which has been called the “Serengeti of the sea” for its incredible diversity of marine life. The Center offers a deeper dive into the research conducted at Long Marine Lab and a chance for everyone to find their inner scientist through rich experiential learning programs including school field-trips, summer youth programs, Science Sundays, volunteer opportunities, internships, and more.Page title
Our History
A Unique Environment
Due to a combination of geological features and currents, the Monterey Bay is one of the richest marine environments in the world. The bay is home year round to harbor seals, southern sea otters, bottlenose dolphins, and two porpoise species. California sea lions, northern elephant seals, northern fur seals, four dolphin species, 13 whale species, and the threatened Steller sea lion come here at different times of the year. Thousands of different kinds of invertebrates and over 450 different kinds of large marine algae live here, as well as thousands of migratory and resident sea birds, shore birds, and fish.
Hidden under the sea surface is the Monterey Bay Submarine Canyon, larger than the Grand Canyon. Here, deep sea environments are a short boat ride away for both researchers and whale watchers instead of hundreds of miles from shore. All of this led to the designation of the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary in 1992.
UC Santa Cruz Marine Science and Education
When UC Santa Cruz opened in 1965, the marine sciences were a key part of the campus vision. Now, with more than 20 marine education and research facilities located along bay, UC Santa Cruz serves as a major institution studying our coast and ocean. Long Marine Laboratory is the oceanside research facility for UC Santa Cruz’s Institute of Marine Sciences. In 1974, Donald and Marion Younger donated 40 acres of coastal bluff and freshwater lagoon to UC Santa Cruz for the establishment of this marine laboratory and for wetland preservation. The Long Marine Laboratory was dedicated in 1978 to honor contributions made to the university by Joseph M. Long, founder of Longs Drugs.
The first director, Bill Doyle, recognized the value of introducing the public to the lab’s activities and he welcomed a new volunteer program to do just that. He then encouraged the establishment of the Friends of Long Marine Lab, a support group for this new education program.
While housed in a portable classroom, the education program grew to serve over 35,000 visitors a year with a small professional staff and a growing volunteer cadre. In 2000, the Seymour Marine Discovery Center was opened as its permanent home.
The Seymour Marine Discovery Center
After nearly a decade of planning, the Seymour Marine Discovery Center opened on March 11, 2000, giving the public a unique view into the workings of a marine research lab. Through the work of the Center, Long Marine Lab remains the only working research laboratory in California open daily to the public.
Private donations funded nearly all of the project’s $6.4 million cost, including an outstanding $2 million cornerstone gift from H. Boyd Seymour Jr. of San Francisco. Seymour’s gift honored his father, Harry Boyd Seymour (1896-1977), and his grandfather, Arthur McArthur Seymour (1864-1919).
H. Boyd Seymour, Jr., was born in 1926 in Sacramento. He received his BA in Biological Sciences from Stanford University in 1947. A retired Principal of Franklin Resources, Inc., Boyd and his wife, Deborah made their home in San Francisco. H. Boyd Seymour, Jr. passed away in September 2009.
Numerous other donors each contributed gifts of $100,000 or more to bring the Center to fruition. They were Leanore Theriot Hooper and Emmet T. Hooper, Paul and Anne Irwin, David and Rebecca Kashtan, the Kresge Foundation, Anne and Paul Levin, the Joseph M. Long Foundation, Zoe Ann Orr Marcus, Frances B. McAllister, the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Phyllis and Alan Simpkins, Richard and Mary Solari, and the Wayne and Gladys Valley Foundation.

TITLE: Cookie Policy | NYC Water Cruises
This Cookie Policy covers all information collected through https://nycwatercruises.com and/or any associated services, sales, marketing, or events. It also describes how NYC Water Cruises ("we," "us," and "ours") uses cookies and similar technologies to recognize you when you visit our websites. It describes these technologies, their purpose, and your rights to regulate how we use them.
What Are Cookie Files?
As you use a network, cookies — text files containing little bits of information, such as a login and password — are used to identify your machine. To identify certain users and enhance their online experience, specific cookies are utilized. The server creates the data stored in a cookie when you connect. An ID that is specific to you and your computer is attached to this data. Your computer and the network server exchange cookies, and the server examines the ID to determine what information it should provide to you.
Due to state and international regulations, such as the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and the EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), many websites must now request your consent before using specific cookies with your browser and, if you agree, tell you how those cookies will be used.
What Cookies Do You Collect?
We employ both first-party and third-party cookies for many purposes. We refer to certain cookies as "essential" or "strictly necessary" cookies because they are technically necessary for our websites to function. In order to improve user experience on our websites, we can additionally track and target users' interests using other cookies. Through our websites, third parties set cookies for analytics, advertising, and other uses. Here is a thorough explanation.
Session cookies are only utilized when a user is on a website. They are never written to the hard disk; instead, they are kept in random access memory. These cookies are automatically removed at the conclusion of the session. They also support your browser's "back" button.
While many persistent cookies have an expiration date and are immediately deleted when that date is reached, persistent cookies stay on a computer eternally. There are two main uses for persistent cookies:
1. Verification. These cookies keep track of a user's login credentials. Additionally, they simplify login details, saving users from having to memorize site passwords.
2. Tracking. These cookies record several visits to the same website. Cookies are used by us to record specific users' visits, including the pages they view. We can show further services that might be of interest to visitors based on the information we obtain. A user's surfing history on that website is used to gradually create a profile.
Use of Flash Cookies Or Local Shared Objects (LSOs)
Additionally, our websites may employ so-called "Flash Cookies" (sometimes called Local Shared Objects or "LSOs") to gather and store data about how you use our services, prevent fraud, and perform other site functions.
If you would prefer not to have flash cookies saved on your computer, you can use the tools in the Website Storage Settings Panel to change your Flash player's settings. Flash cookies can also be managed by accessing the Global Storage Settings Panel and following the instructions. These instructions may include how to block flash cookies that are not being delivered by the page's operator, how to prevent Flash LSOs from being installed on your computer without your permission, and how to delete existing flash cookies from your PC.
Please be aware that some Flash applications, particularly those that may be used in conjunction with our services or online content, may not perform as well or at all if the Flash Player is set to block or limit acceptance of Flash cookies.
About Targeted Advertizing
How To Turn Off Cookie Files
You have the freedom to control your online privacy and browsing experience by choosing to accept or reject cookies. Your web browser's settings allow you to accept, reject, or remove cookies at any time. Remember that while you can still use our website if you refuse cookies, some features and sections might not work as intended or may be restricted.
We advise going to the help menu of your browser for comprehensive instructions on modifying your settings, as the procedures for managing cookies differ according on the browser you use. You can also set preferences for various cookie kinds in many browsers, such as those used for advertising, performance tracking, and necessary functionality.
Contact Us

We promise to give you easily comprehensible information so you may make wise choices regarding your online experience. We are here to help you manage your cookie options, comprehend the many kinds of cookies we use, or understand how they affect your browsing.

=== PAGE: https://austinducks.com/safety/
TITLE: Austin Duck Adventures | Safety
Hydra-Terra is proven unsinkable
Details, we have designed the hull in a specific way that we have patented. The engine is in the middle of the vehicle including the radiator in what we refer to as the tunnel. Along both sides of the hull, we have fabricated many box compartments made of aluminum. These are then filled with urethane flotation foam approved by the U.S. Coast Guard. There are no wires, mechanics, or fluids, running into or through these filled compartments. The construction from the top then resembles a large pontoon or sponsons on each side of the engine room tunnel. So in the event of flooding, the only place water can accumulate is in the very center of the vessel, it cannot go freely from side to side increasing stability not losing it. The amount of flotation foam is the entire weight of the vehicle, full weight of all gear, seats, fuel, etc. and then the U.S. Coast Guard calculates each sole aboard is 185 lbs. Or about 5 tons. Then we add a reserve above this amount of generally 1,000 lbs. so when we remove all the drain plugs and allow the water to free flood the center tunnel, with full load of passengers aboard, we are still about 8" ABOVE the water line and passenger's feet are still dry. If you were to take a saw and run it down the entire side of the vessel cutting into the compartments, it will still not take on water as the foam is in place.
Seaworthiness
The Hydra-Terra has a patented design of the hull that is unique to us. Our center of gravity is exceptionally low. This translates into safer operations on the water. In fact our vessels are all rated at partially protected waters for the U.S. Coast Guard stability. Protected waters are defined below by the U.S. Coast Guard where we typically could go out as far as 20 miles from shore. Exposed Waters - These normally include vessels on an Oceans or Coastwise Route. Partially Protected Waters - Includes vessels on a Limited Coastwise route, not more than 20 miles from a harbor of safe refuge. Protected Waters - Includes vessels on certain lakes, bays, sounds and ICW. No DUKW has a rating above protected waters.
Freeboard
This is really important, fully loaded with passengers our distance from the water up to the top rail of the sides is 4 full feet! DUKW's have something like 16 to 18 inches. I think (never measured exactly). We have taken the inspectors from N.Y. district in NYC out on the Hudson river and they wanted to have me demonstrate seaworthiness. So they arranged for 2 of the big N.Y. Waterways ferries to turn maximum wake and do figure 8's around us as we sailed up the river against current. The waves easily exceeded 10 feet high! No water came into the boat even in these extreme conditions.
Passenger Safety
All highway and Texas Parks and Wildlife regulations are followed. Our vehicles are all inspected during their manufacture to assure all federal regulations for passenger safety are installed. Passenger escape, access doors, isle widths, distance from seat to door are all included in the approvals we have. DUKW's had grandfather protection The old DUKW's had numerous special exemptions from a law called a NAVIC. and the isle ways are much smaller, doors are smaller, emergency egress is more difficult than our vehicles.
Hull material is aluminum
Our hull is marine grade aluminum. OLD DUKW's are very thin steel subject to rusting in water environment.
Hull superstructure engineering
Our hull is designed to international standards adopted by many governments including the U.S. Coast Guard. ABS high speed craft rules are written by a society of naval engineers to assure safe vessel construction. The design for our Hydra-Terra had to be fully inspected and approved PRIOR to any construction of the hull. There are countless calculations performed on the design. What we did was engineer and design the hull ourselves. Then we hired an outside naval architect firm to again run all of the numbers engineering wise for stress as well as stability of the vessel. Only then after their full review, did we submit to the Coast Guard our hull plans. Their procedure is to also completely review all drawings, design, materials, welding procedures, and material testing, etc themselves and not relying of anything submitted for approval. Our hull was fully signed off from the U.S. Coast guard as meeting all requirements of "T" boat regulations. These are the current laws for all commercial vessels. We comply without any such NAVIC exemptions. In addition to all of the above, we had the design put into the super computers for a full finite element analysis. This is the same thing supersize ships are tested with like supertankers. We passed with no modifications required.
Modern Components
The vehicles we manufacture are built with all current mass produced technology. We utilize all new components and meet the model year DOT requirements. So all of the anti-lock braking systems for example are installed just like any new bus on the road. There is nothing old or used in the construction, we do not take old vehicle VIN numbers and "rebuild" an old vehicle side stepping new standards in effect.
Emissions
We use current engines and all that they entail which means we install the DPF exhaust systems in their entirety. Keeping the environment clean is all of our duty.

Can a person with physical disabilities rent one of your boats?
We warmly welcome all guests, including those with physical disabilities, to enjoy our services at Newport Fun Tours. However, please note that our dock and electric boats are not fully accessible. NEGLIGENT OPERATION
If you are not familiar with the term “negligent”, it basically means you are not paying proper attention or acting responsibly while you are operating your boat. There are important rules you need to follow. These rules are to help keep you and your passengers safe. And strictly enforced “Negligent Operation” of a boat is a criminal offense.
Here are a few examples of “negligent behavior”:
Failing to make sure that children 12 years of age and under are wearing a life jacket.
Riding on the bow(front of boat), seat backs (back of boat) of the boat, port side(left side) and starboard (right side)edges of the boat.
Using hazardous towing of Stand-up paddleboards or Kayaks
Operating a boat under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Don’t take a chance with this one.
As an operator of a boat, you are responsible for following the rules. If you allow anyone of your passengers to act in a “negligent” manner, you may face severe penalties.
CHILDREN ON A BOARD
Children on board require special attention.
A life jacket for children 12 years and under is required to be used at all times while boating.
We recommend that a responsible adult is assigned to keep track of each child and their safety and to make sure they are seated before the boat is in operation.
CONTROLLING THE BOAT-HOW TO
BASIC NAVIGATION
There are simple navigation rules to help avoid collision with other boats.
When crossing the path of another boat, you should yield to the boat on your right, (starboard).
When you meet another boat head-on, you should steer to the right (starboard).
When you overtake another boat, you should pass on the left (port) side, leave plenty of room, and yield (give way) to that boat. If conditions require it, you may pass on the right (starboard) side.
If you or the other boat fail to act, and there is a threat of a collision, it is your responsibility to slow down, steer away and/or stop.

You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

INFORMATION ON THE SOS EXPERIENCE

It’s impossible not to get lost! The real question is: will I find my way back? No need to worry. Just shout SOS and a member of the longshoremen team on rollerblades is always ready to help an adventurer in trouble!
Absolutely! At SOS you learn while playing, and all the learning happens through experience, fun, and action. “The Adventure”

HISTORY
Hmmm… That depends on the year you were born!
First, there was SOS Labyrinthe, at King-Edward Pier from 1991 to 1998. This maze of more than 45,000 sq. ft. had the theme “The Mystery Cargo.” This original concept offered the public of all ages a series of learning experiences in a wacky environment, all animated by a team of hilarious roller-skating sailors. SOS Labyrinthe closed its doors in 1998 to make way for the Science Centre.
In 2001, another promoter set up on the 2nd floor of Hangar 16, taking over the essential concept of the maze. The “Labyrinthe du Hangar 16” carried on the tradition for 11 years before closing its doors in 2011.
And finally, the grand return of SOS Labyrinthe took place in 2015, at Hangar 16, to everyone’s great delight!
THE CREATOR
The entire concept of SOS Labyrinthe is the work of Mr. Paul Chartier, grand master of games. He is also the designer of the MayaVentura adventure, the maze at the Just for Laughs Festival, and Safari Missions at Parc Safari.

TITLE: FAQ
Below you will find a few of the most frequently asked questions about our karting facility. Most answers can be found here but if there is something that you are still unsure about, feel free to contact us!
Frequently Asked Questions
Where is Finishline located?
Finishline Performance Karting is located at 1782 Beach Blvd, Biloxi, MS, 39531. Right across highway 90 from the beach and Slap Ya Mommas BBQ.
What are Finishline's operating hours?
What is the admission cost to go to FPK?
Admission to FPK is free of charge if you are just here to spectate. There is cost for the karting, merchandise, arcade, and food. Ride pricing can be found on our pricing page by .
clicking here
How old do you have to be to race at Finishline?
The age requirement for Junior Karts is 8 and older, and there is a 14 year old age minimum for the faster Adult Karts. We have a height requirement of at least 48” for Junior Karts and 60" for Adult Karts. The ages for our Mini Karts is 4-7.
How tall do you have to be race at Finishline?
All Junior drivers or passengers must meet our 48” height requirement (4’) to race or ride on track and atl east 8 Years Old. Adult kart drivers must meet the 60" height requirement and be at least 14 years old. If your child is not tall enough, no problem, we have a full arcade to keep the kiddies entertained or they can ride our Mini Karts! Mini Kart drivers will need to be between ages 4 and 7.
Can a child ride with an adult at Finishline if they do not meet the minimum height requirement?
No, any child that does not meet the height requirement of 52” will NOT be able to ride or drive our go karts. This rule applies to our double karts as well.
How much does it cost to race at Finishline?
Our standard pricing is as follows and does not include tax.
Adults: Juniors:
One Ride $29.99 One Ride $21.99
Two Rides: $49.99 Two Rides $36.99
Double Karts:
One Ride $42.99
Two Rides: $49.99
Can you split the ride packages between customers?
No, the ride packages are based only on a single rider. They cannot be split between customers.
Do you offer any discounts or specials?
Yes, we offer a standard 10% military and first responder discount off of our normal posted rates!
What is the maximum weight and height to race at FInishline
The maximum weight for our adult karts is around 350 lbs and max height is around 7’
Do you need a drivers license to race at FInishline?
No you do not need a drivers license to race at Finishline.
Do you need a reservation at Finishline to race?
A reservation is not required and most of our business is conducted through walk ins. If you have a group of 8 or more, we would recommend reserving a group event with us to run with your group of people. Our arrive and drive is first come, first serve. We cannot guarantee that your group will all be in the same race.
How many laps is each session at Finishline?
Generally 10 minutes of race time is provided.

TITLE: Whale Watching FAQ | Cape Cod, MA | Captain John Boats
Whale Watching FAQ
Captain John Boats has a 99% success rate for seeing whales on all our trips! In the rare instance we don’t see a whale, we will provide a complimentary pass for you to join us on a future trip of your choice. We do not offer cash refunds.
All our boats are equipped with men’s and ladies’ restrooms, regularly cleaned and maintained by our crew.
The temperature on the water is typically about 10 to 15 degrees cooler than on land, so you will likely want to bring a light sweatshirt or jacket, even if it’s warm on land. You may also want to pack a rain jacket in case the weather takes a turn. Other things you’ll want to bring include a camera to get great shots of the whales, binoculars for a closer view, sunglasses, and sunscreen. We recommend wearing sneakers or closed-toe shoes aboard the boat for safety reasons.
Our whale watching tours typically last from 3 hours to 4.5 hours, depending on the location of the whales. We want to give you a good amount of time to spend in the presence of these majestic creatures, so the total tour time varies depending on how long it takes us to get to the whales’ location.
Our whale watching tours involve heading out to Cape Cod Bay and Stellwagen Bank, a marine sanctuary and one of the primary feeding grounds for humpback whales, finback whales, pilot whales, minke whales, and the endangered right whales. Our naturalists will tell you more about these types of whales throughout the tour, identifying which species of whale you are viewing and providing educational information about their habits. We offer full galley service on board where you can purchase hamburgers, hot dogs, pizza, and a variety of snacks. Hot and cold beverages are available, and those 21 and over can purchase alcoholic beverages. Our state liquor license prohibits you from bringing your own alcohol on the boat.
We only offer snacks and full bar service on Pilgrim Belle Cruises. We have a full snack bar on all other boats.
We have different rates for whale watching tours from Provincetown and whale watching tours from Plymouth. Check out our and pages for more information on rates and how to book a whale watching tour.

Josh Brown has been working at Captain John as a deckhand since the age of 17 where he quickly took an interest in the industry and pursued his captain’s license. Kenny Hyslop has been working at Captain John as a deckhand since the age of 13 after a field trip sparked his interest in fishing. Lisa Burke started with Captain John Boats as an intern in 2012. She graduated from Massachusetts Maritime Academy in 2015 with a Bachelors of Science in Marine Transportation. Lindsay Hirt, a Plymouth native, loves her salty hometown so much she decided to make a full circle back here to work after about a decade of academic study and field research along both poles of the eastern seaboard. Lindsay is a marine biologist with a focus on wildlife emergency management and a fondness for teaching others, especially kids, about environmental conservation. She is trained in wildlife rescue for both land and marine species. Over the course of her career, she has interned, volunteered, or worked directly with a wide range of conservation groups, including the National Marine Life Center, International Fund for Animal Welfare, Whale and Dolphin Conservation, New England Aquarium, and the Goldenrod Foundation. The deciding factor for becoming a marine biologist was one Lindsay will never forget- seeing her first whale on a Captain John Boat at age five! She hopes you’ll be just as inspired after an amazing day on the water watching whales.
Michelle Collins comes to us from the fine state of Illinois. She graduated in 2012 from the University of Illinois with degrees in Integrative Biology and Psychology. Just after graduation, she came to Plymouth as an intern on Captain John, started working on the whale watches and has been onboard every season since! After spending almost a decade working in marine mammal conservation, Michelle now works in science communication for the Commonwealth. When she is not onboard, you can find Michelle with her two favorite dogs, crafting, and trying to keep up with Taylor Swift. Michelle loves seeing whales every summer and is excited to see what the next season whale watch has in store!
Kelly Coffin was born in Plymouth but spent much of her childhood in the Sunshine State. After receiving a degree in Biology from the University of South Florida she spent the next decade working with marine mammals with much of that being rescue and rehabilitation work. When she made her way back to Massachusetts she delved into the world of wildlife rehabilitation and kept up with her love of marine mammals by volunteering with local organizations such as the National Marine Life Center and IFAW’s Marine Mammal Rescue Team and by joining the Captain John Boats in 2019. In the off-season she travels around the world participating in rescue, rehabilitation, research and conservation projects for numerous conservation organizations. She also enjoys swimming with humpback whales in their breeding grounds of the Silver Bank after watching them feed all season long here on Stellwagen Bank.
Hailing from Boston, Lisa has always loved whales and the ocean from a young age. She has worked in the environmental conservation field for a number of years, ranging from whales to turtles. As much as she loves whales she will get equally excited pointing out sea birds, especially ospreys and northern gannets. When not on board she enjoys hanging with her 2 pups, kayaking and listening to true crime podcasts.
Mike Hickey has been working on the water for the majority of his life. Captain Russ Burgess was born and raised in Plymouth, MA. TITLE: About | St. Michaels Sailing Charters
History of St. Michaels Sailing Charters, St. Michaels, Maryland
St. Michaels Sailing Charters History on the Eastern Shore of Chesapeake Bay
Hop Aboard St. Michaels Sailing Charters for your personalized boat tour
Ahoy from the team at St. Michaels Sailing Charters! Providing the most personalized and enjoyable boat tour on the Eastern Shore of the Chesapeake Bay is our top priority.
Pictured to the right are owners GM and Laura Bell. GM has been sailing since childhood and previously taught sailing at the Miles River Yacht Club in St. Michaels, Maryland. His sailing adventures have taken him across the Mediterranean Sea, Mexico, Hawaii, California, the U.S. East Coast from Rhode Island to Florida, the Delaware River, and much of the Bahamas and Chesapeake Bay. He has held a U.S. Coast Guard captain’s license since 2014. Laura also grew up sailing with her family on various monohull sailboats and now has several years of experience sailing Epiphany along the East Coast and throughout the Bahamas. She is also the owner and photographer behind Laura’s Focus Photography.
GM spent several summers serving as first mate to Captain Iris aboard the historic Selina II. In 2025, we are honored to “take the helm” of Iris’s company, Sail Selina, as we continue to grow St. Michaels Sailing Charters. After several seasons operating on Broad Creek, we have moved across the harbor for the 2026 season and beyond, sailing from the same Harbour Inn & Marina dock previously home to the Selina II.
We’re thrilled to offer two unique sailing experiences: a historic journey aboard our 1935 ketch, Lady Patty, or a modern adventure on our 44-foot luxury catamaran, Epiphany. Both yachts can accommodate up to 13 guests.

Safety & Restrictions
Are the boats easy to drive?
Yes! Driving our electric boats are on par with driving a golf cart and cruise at around 7 mph. Designated drivers must be 21 years or older and have watched our safety video. The captain (driver) will watch a short safety video and receive a tutorial from one of our expert Crewmembers before setting out. Each boat is equipped with a detailed map so that you can plan your cruise on the lake.
How much of Lake Union will we see?
That is entirely up to your party. There are two designated “trails” on our maps that each take just about two hours. However, you can choose how much time and how fast you tour the lake.
Can we play music on the boat?
Yes! All boats are equipped with Bluetooth.
Who can drive the boat?
Anyone can drive the boat if they are over the age of 25 and have watched our safety video.
How many passengers are allowed on a boat?
We have three kinds of boats: Standard Boat (maximum 10 passengers), Luxury Boat (maximum 12 passengers), and Donut Boat (maximum 6 passengers).
The passenger limit is not based on weight, but on the Coast Guard Certification for our boats. Children count as passengers. This is not a company policy that can be flexible.
Is there an age limit to be a passenger?
There is NO age limit. Everyone is welcome on our boats!
Do the canopies come off of the Standard and Luxury boats?
The overhead canopies must remain on the boats at all times, but you are welcome to raise the side enclosures to feel the breeze! A Crewmember will be happy to help you raise the enclosures before you head out on your cruise.
What can I bring with me?
You are welcome to bring any food or beverage. We rent coolers with ice for $10 and also offer a variety of .
catering options
Will I get cold on the boat?
All of our Duffy electric boat rentals (Standard and Luxury boats) have full window enclosures that can go up or down depending on what you feel comfortable with. If you keep all the windows down the boats stay extremely insulated and warm. During the cold season, we provide heaters for the boats to ensure you are comfortable.
Our Donut Boat and Electric Catamaran options are open-air and are only available during the summer months.
Will my kids have fun?
Absolutely! The Electric Boat Company is a kid-friendly environment. There is plenty to see on the lake and you are welcome to bring games or anything else to entertain the little ones. We are currently working on tablet-based games that you can take out on the lake to entertain any children on board and teach them about boater safety and the lake. Stay tuned for more details.
Can I load and/or decorate the boat while I wait for the rest of my party to arrive?
Usually, but it is not something we can guarantee. If we are sold out, we might not have a boat to let you get into early. Please call ahead if this is something you want to do. You are expected to take all decorations off the boat when you leave.
Are there restrooms on the boats?
No. However, there are a number of restaurants and public docks on the shore where you can disembark and use their facilities. These locations are indicated on our maps. We remind our guests to ONLY PARK AT PUBLIC DOCKS. This is for you and our boat’s safety.
We also have ample restrooms on site at our facilities.
Is The Electric Boat Company open on holidays?
For the most part, yes. Our hours are posted on our website and are subject to change depending on the season. Please contact the office for further detail. We are open rain or shine!

When do I pay for my reservation?

What is the cancelation policy?

Please note, your reservation will not be canceled and refunded for weather unless you have been contacted by a manager. You will be expected to still arrive at the time of your reservation. Lake Union is very protected and inclement weather is rarely an issue. In the case of last-minute unexpected events on your side, refunds will not be provided.

Explore Lake Union in search of clues, solve riddles and lead your team to victory all from within the comfort of our electric boats! Tour Seattle by Boat
Looking for fun activities to do in Seattle year-round, regardless of the weather? The Electric Boat Company launched a Seattle boat tour on Lake Union. FAQ’S
WHAT TIME SHOULD WE SHOW UP FOR OUR CHARTER?
Please arrive 30 minutes before you charter departs. For example, if your charter trip leaves the dock at 8:30, please be here by 8:00.
WHERE ARE YOU LOCATED?
5400 North Ocean Drive in Hollywood Florida –
Directions HERE
WHAT SHOULD WE BRING?
Please bring food and drinks. Also, if you are chartering during the day, remember your sun screen, hats, and sunglasses. Also, bring jackets in case it’s raining or chilly. Don’t forget to bring a waterproof camera.
WHAT DO YOU PROVIDE?
We supply all licenses, tackle, fuel, bait (dead bait included, live bait is available for sale or to catch during the charter), coolers, ice, and decades of experience. All charter trips feature a captain and mate.
WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SPORTFISHING AND DRIFT FISHING TRIPS?
is done 100% on our recently-upgraded large party boat, the “Lois Ann.” This is a shared charter with up to 60 people that fishes daily at 8am, 1pm and 7pm. is a more private and exclusive hands-on offshore fishing experience aboard our custom sportfishing boats in which we target the largest big-game fish in South Florida and some of the most-prized in the world. DO WE NEED TO BUY FISHING LICENSES?
No. You are not required to purchase a State of Florida fishing license when you book a fishing trip with us.
CAN I BRING ALCOHOL ON THE BOAT?
Are you 21 years of age or older? If so, then yes, you can bring alcohol aboard. Are you under 21? Not so much.
HOW MANY PEOPLE CAN I BRING?

ARE THERE ANY AGE REQUIREMENTS?
There are no age requirements. All ages and skill levels are welcome, especially Junior Anglers.
HOW MUCH FISHING EXPERIENCE DO I NEED TO BOOK A TRIP?
None. We provide all the experience that you need. We love teaching others about our sport and coaching you through it all. We have many people who have never fished a day in their life, but leave with a new understanding and a unforgettable experience.
WHAT DO YOU TYPICALLY CATCH?
Fishing always varies from season to season. The best way to see what we’re catching is to keep tabs on our fishing reports HERE. For big game fishing, be sure to check out our shared sportfishing and private sportfishing charters.
DO WE CATCH EDIBLE FISH?
Some of the fish you are likely to catch are edible, and are yours to keep. Generally, if the fish do not have table value, we release them or, in some cases, use them for bait.
DO YOU ACCOMMODATE PERSONS IN A WHEELCHAIR OR WITH RESTRICTED MOBILITY?
Absolutely. Our boats have a flat deck (cockpit) in the back that allows for easy wheelchair access and ability to fight fish. Our crew will help you get on and off the boat.

This happens quite a bit for our clients! We have a great local taxidermist here in town, and they create incredible replica mounts. DO YOU OFFER BIRTHDAY PARTY FISHING TRIPS FOR KIDS?
Absolutely! Our boats and crew are ideally-suited to keep junior anglers busy and comfortable for an unforgettable birthday on the water! Click HERE for more info.
WHAT IS YOUR CANCELLATION POLICY?
Cancellations must be made at least 30 days in advance. Once you are within 30 days, there are absolutely no refunds. No shows are also non-refundable. All sales are final.

WHY BOOK US
Not all charter operations in the South Florida area operate as ethically as we do at Lady Pamela Sportfishing. When deciding on who to fish with, it is important to know before you book your trip and shop for the best price (yes, we price match too!):
We are in the closest proximity to Port Everglades Inlet and the offshore fishing grounds. This means you get more time fishing and less time getting to and from the fishing grounds. Our competitors can take as much as 4 times longer to get you to the fishing areas, thus reducing your opportunity for the great catch.
All of our boats are top notch luxury sportfishing boats. Each and every boat features A/C, Bathroom, Ice and plenty of cockpit area for your party. Don’t get fooled by our competition and wind up on a small, old and worn boat just to save a couple of bucks.
Captain David is on the water daily, sometimes running 2 to 3 trips each day. This allows the Lady Pamela Team to know exactly where the fish are biting and put you on the bite before other boats. (Think the movie “Groundhog Day”)
Captain David is a FULL-TIME charter boat captain (one of very few in area). He does not have the distractions of a day job and his passion is putting people on fish and providing an all-around good time on the water! He’s been on the water all week with customers and knows where the fish are biting and knows what the fish are biting. This allows Captain David to put you on the fish sooner. Time is money. We deliver VALUE. Spend less time looking and more time catching!
David is the owner and operator. In most cases, you will speak directly with Captain David when booking the trip or one of his highly-qualified crew. David does NOT run a booking service as a middleman. When you book with us, you will be fishing with a Lady Pamela Coast Guard Certified Captain on Captain David’s boats using Captain David’s tackle and Captain David’s bait unless you require a multi-boat charter. (Do you see what we mean?)
Our boats, tackle and equipment are all top-notch to make the most out of every bite. Captain David takes pride in his charter service and puts his reputation on the line with each charter. Every minute of every hour of every day.
Captain David does not work with a booking service that takes enormous fees. He books all trips himself and relies heavily on repeat customers like YOU. This ensures you get the most quality fishing trip every time you book. We want everyone to be so pleased that they come back. We are not a “churn and burn” operation that only cares about booking the trip. We deliver VALUE.
Many charter boats in South Florida sell the fish that you catch. BEWARE! All fish you catch within regulations are yours to keep. Captain/crew clean and pack the fish nicely for you. Our crews prefer to practice catch and release to sustain species but you have the final say on all of your legal catches.
Captain David does not get mad or turn into Captain Ahab at the first lost fish or broken tackle. We have heard horror stories about other captains around the docks. David is very easy-going and looks forward to fishing with you and giving you the experience of a lifetime. Captain David even allows you up in the bridge to watch the bite as it happens!
Captain David offers charters specifically-tailored to children and junior anglers so as to introduce our future anglers to the best sport in the world. Captain David takes great pride in keeping children engaged throughout the trip. Captain David would be honored to put your child on the fish of a lifetime.

TITLE: What Makes Dolphins So Smart? Find out on a SeaRacer Dolphin Tour
If you’ve ever been lucky enough to spot a dolphin gliding through the waves off Myrtle Beach, you’ve probably noticed how playful and curious they seem. At Sea Racer Dolphin Tours, we often hear guests ask,
The answer is a big yes! Dolphins are among the most intelligent creatures on the planet, known for their advanced communication, problem-solving skills, and strong social bonds. Let’s dive into what makes these ocean animals so incredibly smart—and why seeing them up close on a is such a special experience.
Sea Racer Dolphin Tour
One of the clearest signs of intelligence in the animal kingdom is brain size and complexity. Dolphins have large brains relative to their body size—second only to humans in some species. Their brains have a highly developed neocortex, the part responsible for reasoning, emotion, and problem-solving.
While dolphins don’t build cities or use tools like humans, their communication, memory, and social intelligence are on par with some of the smartest primates.
Dolphins can even remember individual humans and respond to familiar voices or actions, especially in repeated interactions.
This means dolphins can:
Understand complex concepts
Remember experiences and locations
Learn new tricks or behaviors quickly
When you see dolphins riding the Sea Racer’s wake or jumping alongside the boat, it’s not random — it’s a combination of curiosity and play, both signs of a highly developed mind.
Dolphins don’t just make random squeaks and clicks — those sounds actually carry specific meaning. Researchers have found that each dolphin has its own signature whistle, like a name, used to identify itself to others.
They use body language, tail slaps, and echolocation (a natural sonar system) to share information and navigate the ocean. During our Sea Racer dolphin cruises, guests often hear these high-pitched sounds through the water — a reminder of just how social and talkative dolphins really are!
In studies and in the wild, dolphins have been seen working together to solve challenges — from hunting strategies to protecting one another from predators.
They even use tools! Some wild dolphins use marine sponges to protect their noses while digging for fish in sandy seabeds. This kind of innovation shows creative thinking and adaptability — qualities that make dolphins stand out among ocean life.
Dolphins form close friendships within their pods, and scientists have observed behaviors that suggest they experience emotions such as joy, grief, and empathy.
They’ve been known to help injured pod members or even other species in distress. This deep emotional intelligence is part of what makes seeing them in their natural environment — like off the coast of Myrtle Beach — so inspiring.
You’ll often see dolphins surfing waves, tossing seaweed back and forth, or leaping out of the water near the Sea Racer. This isn’t just for show — play is a vital part of how dolphins learn and build relationships.
Playful behavior is closely linked to intelligence in many animals, and dolphins are some of the ocean’s biggest fun-lovers.
At Sea Racer Myrtle Beach, we believe the best way to appreciate dolphin intelligence is to see it up close — naturally, respectfully, and in their ocean home. Our high-speed Sea Racer Dolphin Cruise gives guests a front-row seat to these incredible behaviors without disturbing the animals.
You’ll witness firsthand how dolphins communicate, interact, and play — proof of their remarkable minds.
Dolphins are more than just friendly faces in the ocean — they’re intelligent, emotional, and deeply social creatures. When you join Sea Racer Myrtle Beach, you’re not just taking a boat ride — you’re getting a chance to observe one of the smartest animals on the planet in their natural habitat.

messages.content:
You extract facts about a local experience business from its own website pages, into a fixed form.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.
- Every offering and fact carries the URL of the page it came from.
- gaps: what a guest would still have to ask, e.g. "age minimum not stated".

Recreation Fee Projects
How Recreation Fees Are Spent
Your Fee Dollars at Work
Thirty National Wildlife Refuges charge an entrance fee and many more charge expanded amenity fees for things like hunting, boat launches, and other specialized recreation. The Federal Lands Recreation Enhancement Act (FLREA), codified as 16 USC 6801 et seq, allows the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to collect and retain revenue from recreation-related activities or facility use. The law requires that funds from this revenue be used to enhance visitor experiences. At least 80% of the funding from recreation fees stays at the site where it is collected, and the remaining 20% is used to benefit sites that do not collect fees or which generate only a small amount of revenue.
Sites that charge fees are required to spend the money to benefit visitors, but in some cases they may hold funds from year-to-year in order to accumulate enough money to accomplish a large project. This site contains information about specific expenditures at wildlife refuges and hatcheries across the country. The intent is to help members of the public understand where these funds are being spent, how much is being expended each year at each site, and how the expenditures are used to benefit visitors.

Federal Recreation Passes
America the Beautiful Federal Recreation Passes
Get an Annual or Lifetime Pass
Your ticket to more 2,000 federal recreation sites! America the Beautiful - National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes give U.S. citizens and visitors an affordable and convenient way to access federal recreational lands. Most America the Beautiful Passes can be purchased as a plastic card, as a digital pass for use in your digital wallet, or both.
Purchase America the Beautiful Pass
Learn About Digital Passes
Types of Passes
Passes can be purchased online or in person at a federal recreation facility. By purchasing passes at your local site, you ensure that the funds from your purchase support projects at that site.
A pass covers entrance and certain day use and amenity fees for the pass owner and all occupants in a personal vehicle at sites that charge per vehicle or, the pass owner and up to three additional adults (16 and over) at sites that charge per person. Children ages 15 or under are admitted free. Each pass covers entrance fees at national parks and national wildlife refuges as well as some other fees at national forests and grasslands and at lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management, Bureau of Reclamation and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

TITLE: Elephant Ivory FAQs
These FAQs provide guidance on how to legally buy, sell, or otherwise trade in elephant ivory to ensure that our domestic markets do not contribute to the decline of elephants in the wild. It’s important to note that regulations do not restrict personal possession of ivory. If you already own ivory – an heirloom carving that’s been passed down in your family, or a vintage musical instrument with ivory components, those pieces are yours. We know those items created long ago aren’t threatening today’s wild elephants. In addition to the information provided on this webpage, you must also comply with any relevant state laws and all imports and exports must be accompanied by appropriate Convention of International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) documents and meet other U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service import/export requirements.
International Affairs
VIEW A QUICK GLANCE GUIDE
What rules and laws regulate the trade of elephants and ivory?
The U.S. Endangered Species Act classifies African elephants as “
Threatened
” and Asian elephants as “
Endangered
.” Under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES),
African elephants
are included in Appendix I, except populations of Botswana, Namibia and Zimbabwe, which were annotated and included in Appendix II in 1997, and populations in South Africa, which were moved to Appendix II in 2000. All
Asian elephants
are included in CITES Appendix I.
International commercial trade in ivory is prohibited under CITES, and further restricted by the
African Elephant Conservation Act
of 1988 and other laws.
On July 6, 2016, a near-total ban on commercial trade in African elephant ivory went into effect. On March 29, 2024, the Service amended the to help ensure imports of live African elephants into the United States contribute to enhancing conservation of the species in the wild and that live African elephants, captive in the United States, are well cared for throughout their lifetimes. Additionally, the rule increases efficiency of permit application evaluations and provides transparency on how we make permit determinations for imports of African elephants.
4(d) rule of the Endangered Species Act
I own elephant ivory. What can I do with it?
First, you need to determine whether your items are made of or elephant ivory. Such proof can be in the form of a qualified appraisal (see question 17) or other documentation that demonstrates the identification of the species through a detailed provenance of the article.
African
Asian
Note that requirements are stricter for Asian elephant ivory with regard to interstate and foreign commerce. For import, the requirements for African elephant ivory are stricter. All wildlife imported to or exported from the United States must be declared at the species level. Without species identification, specimens may be refused clearance and detained at a port.
If you are not able to demonstrate which species of elephant is involved, you may only be able to engage in activities that are lawful for both species, such as interstate commerce of ivory that qualifies as antique under the ESA.
Is it legal for me to keep my elephant ivory?
Yes. U.S. federal wildlife laws and regulations do not prohibit possessing or display of ivory, provided it was lawfully acquired. There is no certification requirement or process to register ivory items and you do not need a permit from the Service to possess or display ivory for noncommercial purposes. We recommend that you maintain any documentation you have that demonstrates the origin and chain of ownership of the item. We recommend that you provide all documentation to any future recipient of your elephant ivory item. Check to make sure that you are also in compliance with local and state laws.
Can I donate or give away elephant ivory?
Yes. U.S. federal wildlife laws and regulations do not prohibit donating or giving away your ivory item, or receiving an ivory item as a donation or a gift, provided it was lawfully acquired and there is no exchange for other goods or services involved. We recommend that you provide the recipient with any documentation you have that demonstrates the origin and chain of ownership of the items. Check to make sure that you are also in compliance with local and state laws.
How can I tell the difference between elephant ivory and other types of ivory?
the Service’s website.
It is possible to identify elephant ivory from other types of ivory. For more information, visit
Forensics Laboratory
Proceed with caution if you are purchasing ivory. Ask for documentation that shows the species and age of the ivory item you are purchasing. This documentation could include
CITES permits
or certificates, certified appraisals (see question 17), documents that detail date and place of manufacture, etc.
What is the difference between worked ivory and raw ivory?
Worked items include carvings and components of larger finished products such as knife handles, billiard cues, musical instruments, and furniture. Raw ivory means an elephant tusk, or any piece of tusk, the surface of which, polished or unpolished, is unaltered or minimally carved, including ivory mounted on a stand or part of a trophy.
Can I import African elephant ivory items…
No. Commercial import of African elephant ivory into the United States is prohibited.
You may import a worked African elephant ivory item (see question 5) into the United States for the noncommercial purposes listed below if it was legally acquired and removed from the wild prior to the listing of the African elephant under CITES (February 26, 1976):
As sport-hunted trophies; limited to two per hunter per year
As law enforcement specimens
As genuine scientific specimens
As part of a household move, inheritance, musical instrument, or traveling exhibition
The import of raw African elephant ivory (see question 5) is prohibited :
As part of a lawfully taken personal sport-hunted trophy; limited to two per hunter per year

50 CFR part 17(e)(6)(ii

We do not require an ESA import permit for ivory items imported as part of a household move, inheritance, musical instrument, or traveling exhibition. All ivory items must also be accompanied by a valid CITES document from the country of export's .

Havasu National Wildlife Refuge, originally named Havasu Lake National Wildlife Refuge, was established by Executive Order by President Franklin D. Roosevelt in 1941 for the primary purpose of providing migratory bird habitat.
National wildlife refuges offer us all a chance to unplug from the stresses of daily life and reconnect with our natural surroundings. At Havasu National Wildlife Refuge, you will enjoy several wildlife-related activities like fishing, canoeing and kayaking, wildlife observation and more!
Learn More About Visiting
A great river in a dry, hot land attracts wildlife and people like a powerful magnet. Today, thousands of visitors annually flock to the refuge to boat through the spectacular Topock Gorge, to fish in Topock Marsh, or to hike in the Havasu Wilderness Area.
Learn More About Us
Havasu Refuge offers guided tours once a month on the second Tuesday of the month from November to April from 9 to 11 am. The tours begin at the North Dike parking lot and follow the dike road through restored marsh, cottonwood/willow and mesquite habitat. Guests will learn about the plants and animals that call the refuge home and get a sneak peek on some of the refuge efforts to conserve this precious resource. call 928-259-9632 to reserve your spot.
View Our Tours
The National Wildlife Refuge System is a series of lands and waters owned and managed by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Wildlife conservation is at the heart of the refuge system. It drives everything we do from the purpose a refuge is established, to the recreational activities offered there, to the resource management tools we use. Selecting the right tools helps us ensure the survival of local plants and animals and helps fulfill the purpose of the refuge.
More About What We Do
Our Species
Havasu National Wildlife Refuge is a birding hotspot with 318 bird species relying on the diverse habitat. Coyotes, foxes, and bobcats cross the roads searching for rabbits and mice. Desert bighorn leap nimbly from steep rock faces along one of the last remaining natural stretches of the river, the 20-mile Topock Gorge. Elusive mountain lions roam and thousands of bats emerge from historic mines in the 17,600 acre Wilderness Area.
