TITLE: Tarpon Springs Florida - Spongeorama Cruise Lines
Tarpon Springs Florida
The first settlers in the area now known as Tarpon Springs were A.W. Ormond and his daughter, Mary. They arrived in 1876. They built a cabin near Spring Bayou. J.C. Boyer, an adventurer from Nassau, sailed into the Bayou. He and Mary Ormond were soon married. One year after the arrival of the Ormonds, George Inness, an American landscape artist, discovered the beauty in the Bayou. He and his son, George, Jr., painted the scenes found in the area.Mary was very pleased with her home. She especially liked the great fish that inhabited the Bayou. They would leap into the air and spray water. In 1879, she named the small settlement Tarpon Springs. (Actually, the fish were mullet, not tarpon!) In 1880, Hamilton Disston, a wealthy saw manufacturer, bought four million acres of the central west coast of Florida from the Governor for 25 cents an acre. This saved the state from bankruptcy. Included in the purchase was Tarpon Springs.In 1884, a post office was established in Tarpon Springs. Soon the railroad arrived and a depot was built to accommodate passengers and freight. Through the efforts and investments of Disston, Tarpon Springs was fashioned into an exclusive winter resort for wealthy Northerners.In 1887, Tarpon Springs was incorporated. It had a population of 52 residents. John Cheney, a promoter associated with Disston, discovered money could be made by harvesting the sponges growing in the waters of the Gulf. Although Tarpon Springs was successful as a resort, it wasn’t long before the sponge industry became the community’s most important industry.By 1890, the sponge industry was firmly established in Tarpon Springs. The Cheney Sponge Company sold almost a million dollars worth of sponges that year.In the next few years, experienced divers from Greece were brought to Tarpon Springs. By using rubberized diving suits and helmets, they increased harvests. By 1905, over 500 Greek sponge divers were at work using 50 boats.The early sponge divers created a need at the docks for eating places for the boat crews. Then as news of the industry grew, people began coming to the docks to see the sponges. Shops opened so people could buy the sponges and other souvenirs.Sponge buyers created the Sponge Exchange in 1907. A building with a courtyard was erected in which each sponger could store his catch while awaiting the auctions that took place twice a week.With the perfection of deep-sea diving equipment, the dollar amount of sponge harvests continued to increase. Divers were able to go deeper into the sea for longer lengths of time. For 30 years, the sponge industry was the largest industry in Florida—larger than citrus or tourism. Tarpon Springs was known as the “Sponge Capital of the World.”In the 1940s, blight reduced the growth of sponges. By the 1950s, sponging as a profitable industry was nearly wiped out. However in the 1980s, new sponge beds were found. Now, Tarpon Springs is back to being a leader in the world’s natural sponge market. All aspects of the sponge industry are available to view in Tarpon Springs, from the harvesting of the sponges, all the way to the auctions that are now held weekly at the Sponge Docks.In addition to seeing the history of sponge harvesting, visitors can experience the Greek influence. Greek restaurants and shops are scattered throughout the area. Seafood, Greek salads, and pastries are particularly popular. Many visitors attend Greek Festivals. St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Cathedral was modeled after the great Byzantine cathedrals such as St. Sophia Cathedral in Constantinople and is open daily to visitors.Today, Spring Bayou, site of the first settlement, is still a delightful place. Visitors can stroll along the winding streets and see houses that reflect the grandeur of the wealthy who came to Tarpon Springs each year to escape the harsh Northern winters. Tarpon Springs still has a peacefulness and quaint charm.

Booking a jet ski rental in St. Pete Beach sounds like pure fun, right? But before you hit the water, there are key things you need to know to stay safe and get the most out of your ride. Before diving into the fun, let's ensure you know the ropes. Safety and understanding the basics are crucial for an enjoyable ride.
In Florida, jet ski regulations are fairly straightforward but important. You need to know these rules to stay out of trouble. Every rider must have a boating safety certificate if they were born on or after January 1, 1988. This certificate shows you've passed a safety course, which is crucial for your protection and others on the water. Learn more about local regulations here.
Age matters when renting a jet ski in Florida. You must be at least 18 years old to rent, but those aged 14 and up can operate a jet ski. However, anyone under 18 needs parental consent. It's vital for parents to understand these requirements to ensure safety for all. Younger riders should always wear a life jacket and, ideally, ride with an adult.
No wake zones are areas where you must travel at idle speed, creating minimal waves. These zones are crucial for protecting marine life and reducing shore erosion. Look for clear signs indicating these areas, and always slow down when approaching. Ignoring these zones can lead to fines and disrupted marine habitats.
Ready to hit the water? Knowing the best times and how to book easily will enhance your experience.
Timing is everything for a memorable jet ski adventure. Early mornings are ideal when the waters are calm and the beaches less crowded. Weekdays often offer more peaceful rides compared to the busier weekends. Check the weather forecast to ensure a sunny day without surprises, as your adventure depends on Mother Nature's mood.

Jet skiing is fun for the whole family. Many rentals offer family-friendly options, ensuring everyone, from kids to grandparents, enjoys the thrill. Got Questions?
Frequently Asked Questions
All your burning questions answered! From safety measures to booking procedures, find everything you need to know before you embark on your journey.
How many people are needed for a cruise to go out?
Tiki cruises are so much better with friends! That’s why we require 6 islanders to go out. If there are less than 6 people booked for the cruise the day before, we will contact you and reschedule to the closest available time or issue you a credit which can be used to rebook at any time in the future.
Where are you located?
Physically or spiritually? Oh, the boring one.
Our address is 60 Rowes Wharf (directly behind the Boston Harbor Hotel) and the dock our boats depart from can be accessed from Gate B or Gate C.
If you’re having trouble finding us, try taking a look at our pinned story conveniently named “Location”!
Instagram
Is there music?
Now what kind of Tiki cruise would it be without some tunes?! We have a Spotify set up on board ready to play your favorite tropical beats.
On public cruises, the captain is also the DJ. They do take requests, but they reserve the right to deny a request if they believe it will mess up the vibe of the boat. No hard feelings!
On private cruises, you are the DJ. You get full access to the playlist and you can blast your heavy-metal-K-pop mashup all through Boston Harbor if that’s your cup of rum.
How many people can go on each cruise?
Our public events have a capacity of 24 passengers, this gives all our guests plenty of room to sit down or walk around the deck. Our private parties can have up to 30 guests.
How old do I have to be to cruise?
To serve drinks on a boat you have to follow quite a few rules, so we can only welcome passengers aged 16 and up on public cruises. But don’t worry, all ages are welcome for private cruises, so bring the whole ohana! Also, just a heads up you have to be at least 21 or older to sit at the bar. Make sure to have your ID ready for a quick check when boarding!
What happens if I’m late?
Short answer – please don’t be! All of our boats run on a pretty tight schedule so we have to depart at the scheduled time. No worries though, we know delays happen and we can always try to hold the boat for a few minutes, but please allow ample time to get to the dock for your scheduled cruise.
If you do end up missing your cruise, we’ll try to put you on another one later in the day, but if we’re unable to do so, your tickets will not be honored. Sorry!
Does the crew accept gratuities?
Islanders are encouraged to tip the crew, not the boat, during the cruise should you feel you’ve been provided with exceptional service. Additionally, you will receive a follow-up email asking about your experience with a link to leave a gratuity if you were blown away. Gratuity is split among the crew that made your experience possible. We highly appreciate any gratuities!
What happens if it rains?
Looking at the forecast and seeing gray? Don’t believe a word they say! We’re kidding of course, but our New England weather is so unpredictable that it’s pretty much impossible to plan too far ahead.
If it happens to be raining at the time of your cruise, it shouldn’t be a problem at all – our boat has a roof and sides that come down so we like to believe it’s always 75 and sunny!
We always keep a close eye on the radar and if the weather does get a bit more extreme (heavy wind, thunderstorm,..) and we do have to cancel, we’ll make sure to notify you as soon as possible and offer you a reschedule or a full refund. Usually, this will be on the day of your cruise.
What should I wear?
A Hawaiian shirt and a Lei, of course. That’s the official Tiki Islander uniform! Basically, wear whatever feels comfortable, but we always advise to bring an extra layer just in case. The temperature in the harbor changes throughout the day so it is better to be safe than chilly.
Can I bring my own drinks?
Unfortunately, since all of our boats carry a liquor license, we can not allow any outside beverages. Don’t worry, our bartender will make sure to keep you well-hydrated!
*Please note, that no beverages or cups can be taken off the boat after your cruise.
Can I bring my own food?
Of course! Feel free to bring your favorite light snacks to enjoy alongside our tropical cocktails.
Just make sure it’s nothing too messy – if there is a mess after the cruise that requires a cleaning crew, we do have to charge a $200 cleaning fee. It hasn’t happened yet, but nobody wants to be the first, so no shrimp cocktail towers or build-your-own taco stations please!
How long is the cruise?
The cruise is in total 1 hour and 30 minutes long. The first 10 minutes is boarding and the last 5 minutes are deboarding.
Is there a bathroom?
Yes, we have a bathroom located at the rear of the boat.
Is there seating available?
Absolutely! We have 12 seats at the bar and another 12 at the front of the boat.
*Seating at the bar is first come, first serve and reserved for customers 21+.
Can I buy drinks on board?
Yes, we have a full bar on board which offers canned drinks as well as tropical cocktails.
What is the cancellation/refund policy?
We know sometimes life gets in the way and plans change. No worries – we got your back! If you need to cancel your booking, we can issue you a credit for the full amount that can be used to rebook at any time (). Keep in mind that a lot of people are eager to cruise with us, so we do require a 72-hour notice for all c!

TITLE: North of the River | Venture Richmond
The General District and Riverfront Overlay Districts
In 1990, the City of Richmond established the Downtown General Special Service and Assessment District to provide special enhanced services in Downtown. The primary district is known as the General District and a map of the area is above. There are also Riverfront Overlay Districts which include the properties along the riverfront and generally south of Byrd Street. ​
Special Service and Assessment Districts, as they are named in Virginia, are similar to Business Improvement Districts (BIDs) which exist in many cities in the United States and around the world. ​
The funding for Richmond’s Downtown enhanced services is provided through a public-private partnership between Venture Richmond and the City of Richmond. The City’s share of the program comes from annual Municipal Services grants, which is the public sector investment. The private sector investment comes from the assessments paid by property owners within the Districts. ​
In Richmond’s General District, comprised of about 440 square blocks on the north side of the river and roughly 82 square blocks on the south side of the river, the property and business owners within the District pay a special assessment of $0.05/$100 of assessed value. In the Riverfront Overlay Districts, there are several districts, and the property and business owners pay an additional special assessment ranging from $0.035/$100 of assessed value to $0.11/$100 of assessed value.
Venture Richmond's Downtown Enhanced Services
Venture Richmond is under contract with the City of Richmond to manage the districts and provide enhanced services to Downtown and the Riverfront districts. Those services include things like:
Providing the Clean and Safe program (sidewalk cleaning, litter and leaf collection, tree well maintenance, weed eradication, etc.
Activating, managing, and beautifying public spaces (Brown’s Island and Canal Walk), landscaping, planters, hanging baskets, etc.)
Marketing and promoting Downtown and its neighborhoods as a place to live, work, play and invest.
Neighborhood placemaking enhancements (bike racks, murals, parklets, etc.)
Promoting economic development and tracking the investment in Downtown
Producing festivals and events that drive visitors to Downtown neighborhoods

=== PAGE: https://venturerichmond.com/our-services/service-district/south-of-the-river/
TITLE: South of the River | Venture Richmond
The Manchester District
Property and business owners in the Manchester neighborhood worked with their neighborhood organizations and Venture Richmond from 2021-2023 on a plan to expand the Downtown General Special Service and Assessment District into Manchester to fund enhanced services and improvements. ​
Manchester is one of, if not, the fastest growing neighborhoods in the city. The private sector has invested over $800 million in the development in the neighborhood, and more is in the pipeline, adding over 5000 residential units (completed or underway). There are new restaurants and new commercial spaces as well. Manchester is generating new tax revenues for the City and the property and business owners are willing to fund enhanced services as part of a public/private partnership with the City. This is a way for the City to reinvest some of those revenues back into the neighborhood. ​
With an expansion of the current Downtown General Special Service and Assessment District, the property and business owners would pay $0.05/$100 of assessed value for enhanced services, just like the property owners in the rest of Downtown. In turn, the property owners have asked the City to be an annual 50/50 funding partner at $400,000. City Council put $300,000 in the 2023 budget as a match to the private sector investment. ​
The planning and conversation regarding enhanced services includes items like:
Expand the Downtown Clean & Safe program to an 80-block area in Manchester and provide consistent sidewalk cleaning, litter pick-up, leaf removal, and weed control and elimination. Power wash homeless hotspots, as needed.
Enhance and maintain tree wells. Distribute pet waste bags in key pet locations; remove pet waste from sidewalks and tree wells.
Strengthen Manchester’s Infrastructure and connections to Downtown.
Assess neighborhood infrastructure needs; advocate for on-street trash cans and bus shelters.
Assess bike rack needs and fund bike racks around the neighborhood.
Work with the neighborhood to develop marketing strategies and a communication plan.
Market and promote retail and restaurants, particularly along the Hull Street corridor.
Advocate for more City Investment.
Work with neighborhood organizations to advocate for safer streets which includes lighting, traffic calming and pedestrian safety, priorities include Hull St. and Commerce Road.
Advocate for City CIP investments in Manchester by engaging the City and developers in planning and determining priorities.

=== PAGE: https://riverqueenvoyages.com/scavenger-hunt-faqs
TITLE: River Scavenger Hunt Tennessee FAQs | River Queen Voyages - River Queen Voyages | Kayak Nashville, TN | Cumberland River Tour
Kayak Quest: River Scavenger Hunt FAQs
What is the Kayak Quest Scavenger Hunt?
The scavenger hunt is a guided, facilitated two hour on-water game from Shelby Park to Riverfront Park. You and your friends, family, team, or co-workers are given a list of clues to solve a crossword puzzle. There are general knowledge clues and clues found on your river paddle. Unscramble a word at the end to win a prize! Learn the history of the Cumberland River and feel like a kid again during this unique and fun adventure. A great way to spend quality time outside making memories, team-building, and having fun on the water. Unbelievable views and photos too!
What is included?
* Scavenger Hunt game
* Shuttle upriver to kayak launch site
* Smartphone drybag
* Gorgeous Nashville skyline views
* Prize for the winner
How many people can go? How much does it cost?
Group minimum is 6 people and maximum is 50 people. The cost is $55/person. Cost includes scavenger hunt clue packets (you can play analog or digital), a phone dry bag ($10 value), RQV sticker ($5 value), and a trained RQV river guide/facilitator. The number of guides and facilitators depends on your group size.
Yes. While same day bookings are sometimes available, we facilitate this adventure with your group so we ask for at least a week of lead time. For this reason, please book online or call us at 615-933-9778 to book and confirm your Scavenger Hunt reservation.
Where do I meet you?
We HIGHLY recommend walking, biking, scootering, or taking a ride share to the as downtown parking is limited and unpredictable. If you are driving, you can try to find street parking near the stadium -OR- you can meet us at the put-in point at (free parking) and we can shuttle you on the back end of your paddling excursion after we have the kayaks loaded back onto the trailers.
Bridge Building / Ghost Ballet
There is often free parking in and around the stadium as long as there are no events going on. Be sure to allow extra time to park and meet the shuttle.
If you are meeting us in Shelby Park, there is plenty of free parking. Groups of 35 or more must provide their own transportation.
*We are not responsible for any parking fees that may occur — please be aware of any no parking signs and allow plenty of time for parking!*
Arrive *at least* 15 mins before your scheduled trip.
The shuttle leaves promptly at your scheduled reservation time and cannot be held for late arrivals. If you arrive late, you can meet us at the put-in location.
The safety of our guests and crew is our top priority. Therefore, we may need to cancel for severe weather threats. Severe weather cancellations may not be made until the start of the tour – we will notify you if made in advance of the trip. Continue reading for our cancellation policy.
I'm new to kayaking, can I still go?
Of course! All of our drivers and river guides are CPR/FIRST AID CERTIFIED and will provide a quick Kayaking 101 and safety demonstration before launching you onto the Class 1 flat water Cumberland River. Regardless of experience-level, Metro Parks, Army Corps of Engineers, and River Queen require that all kayakers wear lifejackets for the entirety of their paddle.
If you would like a tandem kayak instead of a single kayak, please let us know when you make your booking.
What can I bring on the scavenger hunt?
Comfortable clothing and sun protection are always recommended. You can bring your phone as a dry bag will be provided. Small coolers will fit on back of your kayak.
You can leave anything you do not wish to bring or get wet in our shuttle vans and it will be waiting for you at pull-out spot.
*Please know that if you leave items in our van, we are not responsible for anything lost or stolen.*
Yes! Please wear comfortable clothing, shoes that can get wet, and sun protection (hat, sunscreen, sunglasses, etc.). We have dry bags for your phone available as part of the scavenger hunt.
Our kayaks are sit-on-top kayaks so it is normal for a bit of water to splash in but don’t worry; they are also designed to be very hard to sink or flip.
Because this an activity where you will be paddling on a river shared with larger industrial and recreational boats, we do not recommend children under 7, and children under 10 must be in a tandem kayak with parent/guardian. If you wish to kayak with a child under the age of 7, please call us at 615-933-9778.
We allot 2(two) hours for the scavenger hunt but the total length of your experience depends on how strongly and which direction the wind is blowing, how fast the river current moves, and the amount of recent rainfall. Please add an extra hour onto your trip time for shuttling and loading/unloading of kayaks.
Should I tip?
Our drivers and guides definitely appreciate tips! It shows them they did a great job taking care of you by getting you on the river safely and lets them know you enjoyed your experience. 18% is customary and will be added to groups of 6 or more for your convenience. We’ve made it easy to add gratuity online when booking your reservation, or we are happy to accept cash or venmo tips at the end of your paddle.
What is paddling on the Cumberland like?
The Cumberland River is wide and paddles more like a lake so this is an ACTIVE PADDLE, meaning you will be using your arms most of the time. When the river is low and/or the wind is coming from the S/SE/SW, the paddle can be a bit more strenuous than normal.
There is little to no shade on this portion of the river so bring adequate SUN PROTECTION.
The river is a Class 1 flat water commercial waterway so there are no rapids. You will likely share the river with barges, riverboats, fishing boats, and other motorized pleasure craft that can create some small wake. Metro Parks and the Army Corps of Engineers require that you **wear a life jacket at all times** on the Cumberland River.
I have special needs/circumstances. Can I still go?
Call us! 615-933-9RQV (9778). We love to put people on the river!

TITLE: River Queen Pedal Pontoon FAQs | River Queen Voyages - River Queen Voyages | Kayak Nashville, TN | Cumberland River Tour
What is a Pedal Pontoon?
…it’s like a Pedal Tavern, but on the water! Our Pedal Pontoon is a custom built, 16-passenger pontoon boat with a fun twist. (No, you don’t HAVE to pedal!)
While it has a standard motor which can (and often does) solely power the boat, the Pedal Pontoon features 10 bike-style cycle stations which turn the paddle wheel in the back of the boat, making it totally human-powered. The cycle stations are built around a custom teak bar top which includes cupholders at each station and a built-in cooler in the center. This party boat is made for you to eat, drink, and socialize with your group while taking in the breathtaking views of the famous Nashville skyline!
If bike seats aren’t your thing, no problem. We also have some stool seating, benches on the bow, and you are totally welcome to move about the deck and switch places throughout the cruise.
Every tour is driven by one of our USCG-certified Master Captains and assisted by a Deckhand to facilitate your unforgettable adventure.
Need visuals?
Check out our instagram.
Yes! We take reservations 24 hours a day at our website riverqueenvoyages.com. We suggest booking in advance as time slots are limited but can make same-day reservations! We suggest booking as far in advance as possible, especially for weekend time slots. See below for our weather and cancelation policies.
Click here to book your trip now

* 10 Cycle Stations and space for 6 additional seated passengers
* 1.5 Hours of Pedal Pontoon fun on the water
* A Master Captain and a Deckhand to navigate the river and cater to your needs (ask us for fun river facts!)
* A double in-bar cooler for your beverages and plenty of ice
* A top-notch Bluetooth stereo system so you can request your favorite songs
* Emergency marine toilet
* FREE River Queen Voyages famous mermaid souvenir sticker
* Gorgeous views and an unforgettable experience!
How long is the cruise?
Each Pedal Pontoon cruise is 1.5 hours long. This does not include the check-in, orientation, and disembarking. Plan to arrive at our dock check-in location (sent to you upon booking) 20 minutes prior to your cruise start time. We have a tight dock schedule with specific pickup and drop-off times. If you are late to check in we will not be able to board your party and will not issue a refund. Each cruise is on a very strict timeline and cannot be extended. If you are interested in something different than our standard cruise, please text 615-933-9778 or email booking@rqvoyages.com to discuss custom options -- we’re happy to help create an unforgettable experience for you and your group!
We definitely encourage tipping our stellar crew! For your convenience, an 18% gratuity will be automatically added to parties of 6 or more, as well as our private cruises. Our crew works hard to give you a safe, incredible experience on the water and appreciates any gratuity for a job well done. At the end of your journey, if you wish to tip additionally, we also accept cash or venmo tips.
When should I arrive for my cruise?
Please arrive at the dock location to your designated cruise time. Details for the dock location will be sent in your booking confirmation email. Downtown Nashville is BUSY and sometimes roads are blocked so we highly encourage ride share. If you're wondering where to go, your confirmation email has the correct information. Most often the address is (right by Nissan stadium) but if events prevent us from accessing downtown roads, you will be sent the marina location in your confirmation email. Please text 615-933-9778 if you have any questions about the dock location.
The Bridge Building
Downtown Nashville is BUSY so we highly recommend rideshare to 2 Victory Ave Nashville TN 37213 or to the marina location if the downtown roads are closed (always check your confirmation email and day-of communications for the right address).
If you're staying in/near downtown, the docks are located next to the sculpture (red roller coaster looking thing) next to Nissan Stadium. It is also a gorgeous and easy walk over the to get to the docks.
John Seigenthaler Bridge
If you have a car, there is often paid parking and sometimes free street parking around Nissan stadium.
What is your late/no-show policy?
Plan to arrive at our dock check-in location . We have a tight dock schedule with specific pickup and drop-off times. If you are late to check in we will not be able to board your party or issue a refund. Downtown Nashville is busy and roadclosures / traffic happen. Please plan ahead!
We run rain or shine. However, safety is our top priority, and some severe weather conditions could prevent us from operating. Our USCG Master Captain monitors the weather— both radar and onsite conditions— and ultimately decides if it is safe to operate, or if a cruise should be canceled, delayed, or cut short. We do our best to give you time to prepare ormake alternate arrangements, but TN weather can change quickly and sometimes it is not possible.
We do not refund no-shows. Your cruise may be delayed or end early if severe weather is in the area. We will communicate as diligently as possible.
The boat has a canopy that covers 3/4 of it. However, you’re on the water and Tennessee can have unpredictable pop-up storms throughout the season so you may get wet on your cruise. If you choose not to join us due to rainy weather we will not issue a refund.
What is your cancelation policy?
Where do we go on the river?
The Master Captain and Deckhand will take your group from the downtown docks upriver about 5 miles depending on weather/wind conditions. From there you can decide whether to keep going upriver to Shelby Park or stay around downtown! Some great sights are the Omohundro Lighthouse (built 1889), Demonbreun's Cave (cira 1700s), the Metro Nashville goats (if your cruise goes downriver), and of course breaktaking views of the famous Nashville Skyline! The cruise ends back at the downtown docks (or the marina if downtown roads are closed) at the end of your 1.5 hours.
The more you pedal on the boat, the farther your group will travel--so make sure to bring your A-game!
How many people can fit on the boat?
The Pedal Pontoon can accommodate up to 16 passengers and 2 crew members.
There are 10 cycle stations and additional stool and bench seating available, so you can rotate out based on whether you’d prefer to pedal (not required!) or just enjoy the scenery. Didn't get a pedal seat right away? Don't worry! Every shares and it's a blast!
Is there a bathroom on board?
We have an emergency marine toilet on board. It is open aired but we have a pop-up tent if you’re shy! Please allow ample time for using the restrooms at the docks prior to boarding. All boarding locations will have adjacent bathroom facilities available and we highly recommend using the Bridge Building facilities prior to getting on the Pedal Pontoon. We are not responsible if your friends take a picture of you using the emergency marine toilet ;)
Who drives the pontoon?
Our crew drives the boat for you! Included in every reservation is a USCG licensed Master Captain and Deckhand. The RQV crew will ensure your group is safe and has a great time.
What if I have more than 16 people in my group?
Our pontoon capacity is 16 guests but no problem; we are happy to book your group on multiple trips. Please email booking@riverqueenvoyages.com to make large group arrangements.
Can I bring food and drinks?
Pedal Pontoon trips are currently BYOB. ABSOLUTELY NO GLASS ALLOWED. You can bring water, soda, sports drinks, beer, wine, etc. We provide plenty of cooler space for your beverages and plenty of ice so no outside coolers please. You are welcome to bring snacks, sandwiches, or other small food items aboard but again NO GLASS.
Can I bring bags, purses, cameras, etc. aboard?
Yes! However, we have limited storage aboard the Pedal Pontoon so only bring what you need. No large backpacks or other bulky items allowed. No drone

Our gorgeous blue and green single (1 person / 300lb max capacity) and tandem (2 person / 450lb max capacity) kayaks are sit-on-top kayaks. They are made right here in Sparta, Tennessee at Jackson Kayak.
Sit-on-top kayaks are designed to not sink or easily flip. It is normal for a bit of water to splash inside the kayak but need not worry, you wont be going down with the ship in these bad boys! Our Jackson Riviera kayaks are the perfect boat for your river adventure.
What can I bring on the kayak?

What is paddling on the Cumberland river like?
The Cumberland River is wide and paddles more like a lake, so this is an ACTIVE PADDLE—meaning you will be using your arms most of the time. The current is not very fast but there are undercurrents so please be attentive while on the water. When the river is low and/or the wind is coming from the S/SE/SW, the paddle can be a bit more strenuous than normal.
There is little to no shade on this portion of the river, so bring adequate SUN PROTECTION. For a full list items to bring, read our Before You Go page.
The river is a Class 1 flat water commercial waterway, so there are no rapids. You will likely share the river with barges, riverboats, fishing boats, and other motorized pleasure craft that can create some small wake. Metro Parks and the Army Corps of Engineers require that you **wear a life jacket at all times** on the Cumberland River.

What is a Hobie Fiesta 4 person pedal drive boat?
The Hobie Fiesta is a 4-person, pedal-powered boat designed for recreational use. It features Hobie's MirageDrive pedal system, which allows you to power the kayak with your feet instead of a traditional paddle. There is a paddle on board if desired.
How easy is it to learn how to pedal the boat?
It is relatively easy to learn how to pedal the Hobie Fiesta, but it does take some practice to become proficient.The Mirage Drive system works by using a pedal-drive mechanism that propels the fins back and forth. The fins, in turn, propel the watercraft forward. You control the speed and direction of the watercraft by adjusting the angle of the fins and by pedaling at a faster or slower pace. An RQV crew member will provide instructions on how to pedal and steer the Fiesta before your rental begins.

The Hobie Fiesta is steered using the two handlebars located near the pedals. The speed and direction of the Fiesta can be controlled by adjusting the angle of the fins on the MirageDrive pedal system.

TITLE: Snorkeling Tour vs Sandbar Combo in Islamorada: Which to Choose
How to Choose Between Snorkeling Tour vs Snorkeling and Sandbar Combo in Islamorada
Choosing between our 2-hour snorkeling tour and our 3.5-hour snorkeling and sandbar combo comes down to what matters most to you: dedicated versus a more comprehensive Florida Keys experience. The snorkeling tour focuses entirely on reef exploration, while the combo adds sandbar relaxation, making it our most popular option for families and groups with varied interests.
underwater time
The 2-Hour Snorkeling Tour: Pure Reef Focus
Our gives you maximum time exploring Islamorada’s coral reefs. We spend the full 2 hours at world-class locations like Alligator Reef and Cheeca Rocks, where you’ll encounter vibrant coral formations, tropical fish, and often sea turtles.
This tour works best if everyone in your group is excited specifically about snorkeling. You’ll get more bottom time, potentially visit multiple reef sites, and have the flexibility to explore at your own pace without rushing to another activity.
Who Should Book the Snorkeling-Only Tour
Choose the 2-hour snorkeling tour if you’re passionate about , have limited time in Islamorada, or prefer a shorter experience. It’s ideal for dedicated snorkelers, underwater photographers, and anyone who wants to maximize their time among the coral and marine life.
underwater exploration
The focused format also suits younger children who might not have the stamina for a longer trip. Two hours provides plenty of reef time without overwhelming kids who are new to snorkeling.
The 3.5-Hour Combo: Best of Both Worlds
Our delivers the complete Islamorada experience. You’ll spend time snorkeling at spectacular reef locations, then transition to pristine sandbars where crystal-clear, waist-deep water creates a natural swimming pool surrounded by turquoise beauty.
This is our most popular tour for good reason. Ninety percent of our sandbar guests are families, and the format ensures everyone has an amazing time regardless of their comfort level in the water.
Why Families Love the Combo
The sandbar component transforms this from a snorkeling trip into a complete adventure. Kids can run around, play games, use paddleboards, and swim in water that’s cleaner than most hotel pools. Parents can relax knowing children are safe in shallow water while still experiencing the natural beauty of the Florida Keys.
Even guests who struggle with snorkeling or prefer not to participate always have a fantastic time at the sandbar. It’s not just a consolation prize – the sandbar experience stands on its own as a highlight of any Islamorada visit.
Comparing Time and Value
The snorkeling tour runs 2 hours and costs $75 for adults and $65 for children. The combo extends to 3.5 hours and costs $120-135 for adults and $95 for children. That’s an additional 1.5 hours of experience for roughly 60-75% more cost.
When you break down the value, the combo delivers significantly more for your money. You get reef snorkeling plus an entirely separate sandbar experience, all with premium beverages included throughout. Most guests feel the combo represents better value unless they’re specifically seeking only snorkeling.
What’s Included in Each Option
Both tours include professional-grade snorkeling equipment, expert instruction, and complimentary beverages. Our covers what else to bring, but we provide everything essential for the water activities.
The combo tour adds beer, wine, and rum punch to the beverage selection, plus access to paddleboards and floating devices at the sandbar. Our boats also feature onboard music systems, creating a more relaxed, party-friendly atmosphere during the sandbar portion.
Weather and Flexibility Considerations
The combo tour offers built-in flexibility that proves valuable when weather conditions vary. If ocean conditions aren’t ideal for reef snorkeling, we can substitute bayside snorkeling locations or extend sandbar time, ensuring you still have an incredible experience.
The snorkeling-only tour depends entirely on suitable reef conditions. While we rarely need to cancel, the focused format means weather plays a bigger role in the experience quality. Captain Matt always makes safety decisions based on current conditions.
Group Dynamics and Mixed Abilities
If your group includes both enthusiastic snorkelers and people who are nervous about open water, the combo tour solves that challenge beautifully. Confident swimmers enjoy the reef, while others know the sandbar awaits where they can participate comfortably.
The snorkeling-only tour works better for groups where everyone shares similar enthusiasm for underwater exploration. Mixed-ability groups often find one or two members feeling left out during a pure snorkeling experience.
First-Time Snorkelers
Both tours welcome beginners, and our crew provides thorough instruction before you enter the water. often appreciate the combo format because it removes pressure – if snorkeling feels challenging, they know something else fun is coming.
First-time snorkelers
The dedicated snorkeling tour works fine for beginners who are committed to trying, but the combo provides a psychological safety net that helps nervous first-timers relax and enjoy themselves.
Schedule and Timing
Consider your daily itinerary when choosing. The 2-hour tour fits easily into a packed vacation schedule, leaving time for other Islamorada activities before or after. The 3.5-hour combo becomes your primary activity for that part of the day.
Many guests find the combo’s longer duration actually more relaxing. You’re not rushing through experiences or watching the clock. The extended time lets you settle into island pace and fully enjoy both the reef and .
sandbar environments
Which Tour Does Captain Matt Recommend?
After nearly 15 years running charters in these waters, Captain Matt typically steers groups toward the combo unless they specifically request snorkeling only. The combo format consistently generates the most enthusiasm and the best guest experiences.
That said, dedicated snorkelers who want maximum reef time, groups on tight schedules, or families with very young children sometimes find the 2-hour tour better suits their needs. There’s no wrong choice – it depends on your priorities.
Making Your Decision
Ask yourself these questions: Does everyone in your group love snorkeling, or do interests vary? Do you want a focused experience or variety? Are you comfortable with a longer time on the water? Is budget a primary concern?
If you answered “interests vary,” “variety,” “yes,” and “not really,” the combo is probably your best bet. If you answered “everyone loves it,” “focused,” “prefer shorter,” and “yes,” the snorkeling tour might work better.
Still unsure? Call us at and we’ll talk through your specific situation. We’ve helped thousands of guests choose the right experience, and we’re happy to answer any questions. Or check our for more details about both tours.

TITLE: Exploring the Hidden Gems of Ozello FL: Airboat Adventures with Native Captains
Ozello, Florida, offers a unique escape from the usual tourist trails. Nestled in the backwaters near Crystal River, this quiet coastal area reveals a world of natural beauty and rich cultural heritage. One of the best ways to experience Ozello is by airboat, guided by native captains who know the waterways intimately. This adventure combines thrilling rides with deep local knowledge, making it a must for nature lovers and explorers alike.
Airboat cruising through Ozello backwaters with native captain
Discovering Ozello’s Unique Ecosystem
Ozello is part of a delicate ecosystem where freshwater meets saltwater, creating an environment rich in wildlife and plant species. The backwaters are lined with mangroves, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. These habitats support a variety of birds, fish, and other wildlife, including manatees and dolphins that often swim close to the airboats.
The native captains who navigate these waters have grown up in the area. Their knowledge of the tides, wildlife behavior, and hidden channels ensures a safe and informative journey. They often share stories about the local environment and the importance of preserving this fragile ecosystem.
What to Expect on an Airboat Tour
Airboat tours in Ozello offer a mix of excitement and education. The boats are designed to skim over shallow waters, allowing access to places larger vessels cannot reach. The ride itself is exhilarating, with the wind in your face and the sound of the engine echoing across the water.
Tours typically last between one and two hours. During this time, you will:
Glide through narrow mangrove tunnels
Spot wildlife such as herons, egrets, and occasionally alligators
Learn about the history and culture of the native communities
Enjoy panoramic views of the Crystal River backwaters
The captains often tailor the experience based on the group’s interests, whether that’s birdwatching, photography, or simply soaking in the peaceful surroundings.
The Cultural Connection with Native Captains
One of the highlights of exploring Ozello by airboat is the chance to connect with native captains. These guides are more than just pilots; they are storytellers and custodians of local traditions. Many come from families who have lived in the area for generations, passing down knowledge about fishing, boat-building, and the natural world.
Listening to their stories adds depth to the adventure. You might hear about old fishing techniques, legends tied to the land, or the challenges faced by the community in protecting their environment. This cultural insight enriches the experience and fosters a greater appreciation for Ozello’s heritage.
Practical Tips for Your Airboat Adventure
To make the most of your trip, consider these tips:
Wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing.
Lightweight, breathable fabrics work well, and a hat and sunglasses will protect you from the sun.
Carry a camera or smartphone.
The scenery and wildlife provide excellent photo opportunities.
Listen carefully to safety instructions.
Airboats can be fast and loud, so following the captain’s guidance is essential.
Book in advance.
Tours with native captains are popular and can fill up quickly, especially during peak seasons.
Why Choose Ozello Over Other Florida Destinations?
While Florida has many popular water destinations, Ozello stands out for its quiet, untouched feel and authentic local experiences. Unlike crowded tourist spots, Ozello offers a chance to explore nature at a slower pace, guided by people who truly know the area.
The combination of thrilling airboat rides and cultural storytelling creates a memorable adventure that appeals to families, solo travelers, and groups alike. It’s an opportunity to see a side of Florida that many visitors miss.
Supporting Local Communities and Conservation
Booking an airboat tour with native captains also supports local communities directly. These tours provide income and help preserve traditional ways of life. Many captains are involved in conservation efforts, working to protect the waterways and wildlife of Ozello.
By choosing these tours, visitors contribute to sustainable tourism that respects both nature and culture. This approach helps ensure that Ozello’s backwaters remain vibrant and healthy for future generations.

The space program isn’t the only thing that’s out of this world in .

What Is It Like to Fish In Cape Canaveral?
Cape Canaveral deep sea fishing charters benefit greatly from the protection of the federal government. The area is not overfished or otherwise exploited due to 140,000 acres of protected waters. This does result in some limitations, but nothing the average angler would have a problem with. There’s no night fishing from the shore, for instance, and you can’t fish at night in ponds, either, but you can still fish in several areas at night from a boat. There are also size and catch limits.
While this may involve sacrifice on the part of some fishermen, the results are definitely worth it. The area is teeming with a vast variety of fish, both exotic and delicious. You get the conveniences of a 21st-century city like Cape Canaveral combined with the excitement and thrill you get when fishing in a prime Eastern Atlantic location. The weather is pristine with a yearly average of 82 degrees Fahrenheit, and the clouds are few and far between. Even during the rainier parts of the year, such as August and September, the average rainfall is still only a little over 7.5” per month.
Deep Sea Fishing in Cape Canaveral
While all fishing in the area is exciting, deep-sea fishing charters in Cape Canaveral are an adventure in and of themselves. Whether you book a day or a half-day, you are thrusting yourself into a rich environment full of a vast variety of fish. You can grab a bunch of friends and take a full-day charter way out to sea. === PAGE: https://www.kelownadowntownmarina.com/boating-questions.html
TITLE: Kelowna Boat Rental Frequently Asked Questions by Kelowna Downtown Marina
Have questions about the lake or moorage? Ready to rent a boat but have a few questions first? No worries! Here are a few of our most frequently asked questions. If your question isn’t here, please reach out! We’d love to chat with you about any questions or concerns you may have.
Rental
Q: Can I rent a boat without a boater’s license?
Yes! When you rent a boat with Downtown Marina, we’ll supply you with a temporary boater’s license. In addition to that, we’ll give you a full tour of your boat rental and run through all the safety features.
Q: Does insurance cover any damage I accidentally cause?
No, unfortunately, that’s not how it works. When you rent the boat, we’ll run a pre-authorization on your credit card for a set amount. If damages occur, the person that rents the boat is liable. Our team will walk around the boat with you and take lots of pictures during orientation so we are all aware of any existing scratches or damage.
Q: Can I drink before hopping behind the wheel of a boat rental?
No. At Downtown Marina, we have absolutely zero tolerance for driving a boat while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Instead, save those drinks for after you’ve returned your boat rental.
Q: Now that marijuana is legal, can I smoke before or while driving my boat rental?
No. Our zero-tolerance policy for drugs and alcohol also applies to marijuana. Using these substances can impair your driving ability and aren’t safe for you, your passengers, or other boaters on the lake.
Q: How long should I rent a boat for?
Depending on what you want to do on the lake, the time may vary. However, most renters find four to eight hours a sufficient amount of time for most activities.
Q: Does my child count as a person on the boat?
Yes! No matter how big or small they are, every passenger on the boat will be counted, even babies that board the boat in their own portable car seats.
Q: Can I bring my pet on the boat with me?
Of course! We know pets are family, and that’s why we count them as a person when you book a boat rental. Don’t forget to pack some water and a life vest for your pup too!
Q: I’ve never driven a boat before. Can I still rent one?
Absolutely! The team at Downtown Marina is committed to getting everyone out on the water. We’ll give you a full orientation and make sure you feel confident and safe before leaving the dock.
Q: Do I need to bring my own lifejacket?
At Downtown Marina, we supply lifejackets for everyone on board the boat. The only thing you need to bring is yourself, your buddies, towels, water, sunscreen, and snacks.
Q: If I rent a Jet-Ski, can I park it on a beach?
No. Jet-Ski rentals are required to stay on the water and not be parked at a beach. Because of its impeller, Jet-Ski's can suck up sand, seaweed and other debris found on shorelines and this can damage to the watercraft.
Q: Can I anchor my boat rental?
Our boat rentals do not come with anchors. Okanagan Lake is large enough that if you want to float and have a swim, you can do so without anchoring.
Q: Is gas included in the boat rental?
When you rent a boat, your rental will come with a full tank of fuel. When you return it, you’ll be charged to refill it, so you only pay for what you use.
Q: I can’t swim. Can I still rent a boat?
Yes! Your boat rental will include an approved life vest for you to wear in case you end up in the water unexpectedly. We also service our boats daily to ensure your safety.
Q: Do you offer water accessories with rentals?
Yes, we do. You can rent for an additional fee. Accessory rental rates are reduced with the rental of a boat.
additional accessories like tubes, wakeboards and surfboards
Q: How much does it cost to rent a boat?
The . For example, Jet-Ski's typically cost around $169 an hour while a pontoon boat goes for roughly $300 an hour.
cost of a boat rental varies by type
Q: How old do you need to be to rent a boat?
All renters need to be 19 years of age or older, with the exception of Tournament boats. For those, the renter has to be at least 21 years of age.
Q: Do you rent pontoon boats?
Yes! We have a variety of pontoon boats available to rent.
Q: Can I rent a boat for a day, a week, a month?
Yes! You can book rentals online on our website for up to . If you require a boat for a period of time longer than that, please contact us directly.
8 days
Q: If I rent the boat, can one of my passengers drive it too?
Only the renter of the boat is permitted to drive it. But don’t worry, we’ll show you how to operate it and run through any information you need to know before you leave the dock.
Q: What time should I arrive for my rental?
It’s recommended that you arrive 30 minutes prior to your rental period. This allows us the time you’ll need to get you checked in and set up before your rental period begins.
Q: Can we use a pontoon boat for wakeboarding?
No. Pontoon boats aren’t meant for skiing or wakeboarding behind. They’re better suited for boaters hoping to soak up some sun while lounging around and taking in the fabulous lake views.
Q: When can I check in for overnight moorage?
When you book overnight moorage at Downtown Marina, a slip will be available for you from 3 PM on the day you requested until noon the following day. If you need extra time, let us know.
Q: Can I sleep on my boat if I rent a boat slip for a night?
For safety reasons, we don’t allow boaters to spend the night on their boat while it’s tied to our dock. Check out some of the beautiful hotels in downtown Kelowna instead!
Q: Can I park my boat while I go into the downtown core?
Yes! We offer slips for hourly parking. Just pull up, tie up, and pay up. There’s a parking meter right on the dock. Just don’t forget to put your ticket in the window of your boat.
Payment & Cancellation
Q: What is the cancellation policy for a boat or Jet-Ski rental?
Cancellations must be made at least 48 hours in advance. If you fail to show up, the cost of the rental will be applied to your credit card in your absence.
Q: Can I use my debit card, debit Visa or cash as a damage deposit?
For the initial damage deposit, we only accept credit cards. However, once you’ve returned your rental damage-free, you’ll be able to pay for it with whichever method you prefer.
Q: How much is the pre-authorization cost for a boat rental?
For Chaparrals, Pontoon boats, Bayliners, and Seadoos, the pre-authorization fee is $1000 plus the cost of the rental. The pre-authorization fee for tournament boats, Cobalt R5/R6/R7, and the Regal LS4 is $2500, and the fee for kayaks and paddleboards is $250.
Q: Will I still be charged for a rental if the weather is really bad, and I don’t want to go out on the lake?
Unless the weather is totally unfit for boating (thunder and lightning) during your rental period, you’ll be charged for your rental whether you’re there or not.
Other
Q: What are some must-see places on Okanagan Lake?
While there are to visit on the lake, we highly recommend:
many places

Paul’s Tomb
Bertram Creek Regional Park
Q: How deep is Okanagan Lake?
Okanagan Lake has a maximum depth of 232 metres. It’s between 4 and 5 kilometres wide, and it’s 135 kilometres long. It actually stretches from Vernon all the way down to Penticton.
Q: Do boats have brakes?
Boats don’t have traditional brakes like the ones you find in cars, trucks, and SUVs. When driving a boat, you’ll utilize neutral and reverse to control the speed of your boat.
Q: Is it still safe to go boating while it’s raining?
Yes! Our boats are available during most kinds of weather. We will, however, stop you from boating if a serious storm blows in. Thunder and lightning are dangerous while boating.
Q: Is there a speed limit on Okanagan Lake?
Some areas of the lake are subject to speed limits, like passing underneath the Bennett Bridge. Always follow any posted speed limit sign you come across. Failure to do so can result in fines.
Q: Does the lake have police patrol or coast guards?
Yes, Okanagan Lake has police boats on patrol

=== PAGE: https://www.kelownadowntownmarina.com/blog/seadoo-rental-faqs.html
TITLE: Jet-Ski Rental FAQs: Everything You Need to Know | Kelowna Downtown Marina
You’ve just arrived in Kelowna. The sun is shining, the water is sparkling, and you’ve just decided you want to get out on the water and experience true Okanagan living. However, you may not know exactly what’s required of you before lining up wakeboard boats or Jet-Ski rentals. Kelowna lake is calling you, so to make things easier and get you on the water faster, we’ve compiled a list of some of our most frequently asked rental questions.
1. How old do I have to be to take advantage of vacation boat rentals?
There are a few different age requirements for different types of rentals. If you’ve got your eye on a Jet-Ski rental, a Bayliner, a Chaparral, or a Pontoon boat, you need to be at least 19 years of age to sign a rental contract. The same goes for kayak and paddleboard rentals. If you’ve got dreams of wakeboarding behind a MasterCraft, Cobalt R5/R6/R7 or Regal LS4 boat, however, you’ll need to be at least 21 years old before renting one of these.
2. What do I need to provide before booking Kelowna boat rentals?
In order to secure a boat, Jet-Ski, or paddleboard rental, you need to be able to provide a current and valid photo ID and a credit card that can carry a pre-authorization for the rental.
For regular boats (Bayliners, Chaparrals, and Pontoon boats), the pre-authorization cost is $1,000 plus the cost of the rental and applicable taxes.
For wakeboard boats (MasterCrafts, Cobalt R5/R6/R7, and Regal LS4), the pre-authorization amount is $2,500 plus the cost of the rental and tax.
For kayaks and paddleboards, the pre-authorization amount is $250 plus the cost of the rental and tax.
3. Can anyone in my party drive the boat if I rented the boat under my name?
Unfortunately, the renter of the boat is the only person permitted to drive the boat. Before hitting the Kelowna lake, one of our qualified boating experts will explain how to operate the boat and run through any safety precautions to be aware of while on the lake. Boat drivers are not included with boat rentals.
4. Do I need a boat license to operate a boat rental?
No. As a renter, we are able to supply you with a temporary license that is valid for the duration of your boat rental period.
5. Who pays for the boat fuel?
The renter is responsible for paying the fuel costs on their Kelowna boat rentals. When you leave the marina, the boats fuel tank will be full, we’ll top it up on your return, and then charge you only for the amount of fuel used.
6. What is the cancellation policy for a boat or Jet-Ski rental?
Unless the weather is unfit for boaters, a cancellation must be made at least 48 hours in advance. If you fail to show up during the rental period you originally requested, the cost of the boat or Jet-Ski rental will be applied to your credit card in your absence.
Ready to secure a boat rental during your next stay in Kelowna? Check out Downtown Marina. We offer competitive rental rates, top-of-the-line boats and accessories, and one of the best marina locations in the city.

TITLE: Things to do in Denver weekend, Colorado: Attractions, Places, Activities, Tours
THINGS TO DO IN DENVER
Denver, Colorado's capital and largest city provides mile-high fun and 300 days of sunshine for its residents and visitors throughout the year. What it offers includes outdoor activities, such as visiting Rocky Mountain National Park and the Denver Zoo, as well as indoor activities, such as visits to the United States Mint and the Denver Center for the Performing Arts. Several of these attractions are conveniently situated in downtown Denver while others are worth the drive or the taking of public transportation necessary to reach them. Regardless of what interests you have the preponderance of things to do in Denver and near Denver will keep you entertained tomorrow and in other days.
1. Visit Rocky Mountain National Park
One of the features that Denver is most known for is its sitting less than a 30 minute drive from the Rocky Mountains' Front Range. Meanwhile, Rocky Mountain National Park, a 265,000-acre area that is dedicated to preserving much of this beautiful place, is 90 minutes from downtown Denver. It was designated as a national park in 1915, and millions of visitors take in its beauty on an annual basis.
The Continental Divide runs through the middle of it, resulting in a more forested half, which is closer to Denver, and a drier and glaciated half on the other side. Its highest point is Longs Peak, which reaches 14,259 into the sky. Many visiting the park enjoy driving on Trail Ridge Road, which reaches an elevation of 12,183 feet. The easiest way to visit the park would be taking a guided tour from Denver Downtown.
2. Go on the Denver Foothills Tour to see Red Rocks Amphitheatre
One of the best things to do near Denver Colorado is going on the Denver Foothills Tour, of which a visit to the Red Rocks Amphitheatre is a highlight. Also enjoyed on this trip is a breathtaking view from Lookout Mountain, which is also where the Buffalo Bill Museum and Grave is located. Next will be a stop at peaceful Evergreen Lake.
Regardless, the time spent at the Red Rocks Amphitheatre, arguably the most beautiful amphitheatre in the world, is what many remember most from this journey. Those who fill its 9,525 seats get to enjoy live music and other live performances while being able to also gaze up at the large rock formation that stretches from behind the stage to high above the seating area to the left of the spectators.
3. Visit Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway
Visitors looking for things to do around Denver in addition to in the city itself are encouraged to take a drive on the Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway (formerly Mount Evans). This 28-mile road, which can be reached via a 40-minute drive, is a great way for you to fully experience the Rocky Mountains. In fact, it is the country's highest paved road, gaining more than 7,000 feet in elevation and reaching 14,130 feet at its highest point.
As you are making your way into the mountains, you will come across several lookout points, where you can stretch out your journey and take in increasingly impressive views of the Rockies. Many experienced Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway drivers recommend that newcomers take the guided tour and pay special attention to Echo Lake Park, which will be reached at roughly the midway point.
4. Discover Pikes Peak and the Garden of the Gods
A couple more things to do near Denver that you should consider are visiting Pikes Peak and the Gardens of the Gods, both of which are near Colorado Springs, to the south of Denver. Although separate areas, the Garden of the Gods provides a tremendous opportunity to take in a gorgeous view of Pikes Pike.
Within the Garden of the Gods is an impressive group of picturesque red rock formations and a nice collection of hiking trails. In fact, it has such a reputation that TripAdvisor named it the nation's best park, ahead of runner-up Central Park in New York.
Meanwhile, Pikes Peak has an elevation of 14,115 feet and is the highest point in the United States from it to the east. One memorable and comfortable way to climb it is taking a guided tour via the Pikes Peak Highway.
5. Denver Botanic Gardens
If you are looking for things to do in Denver Colorado that are picturesque, a trip to the Denver Botanic Gardens is recommended. It provides a peaceful respite from all of the activities that the city center offers. This oasis of greenery offers 23 acres of theme gardens as well as the UMB Bank Amphitheater, which has a capacity of up to 1,300.
Simply put, this is a place where it is easy to fall in love with its beauty. You can spend hours here browsing its 50 gardens, which range from a traditional Japanese garden to an area that displays plants native to South Africa. Art aficionados will also enjoy the many art exhibits on display here at various times throughout the year. Also note that guided tours enhance many visitors' experiences.
6. Denver Zoo
Another of the nature-focused Denver Colorado attractions is the Denver Zoo. In fact, a Visit Denver survey found that it was the top paid attraction in the city. It is also viewed by many as one of the best zoos in the country. More than 2 million people visit it in a normal year and enjoy seeing and learning more about the 4,000 animals that call this place home.
One of its most memorable attractions is Bear Mountain, which is an area that mimics bears' natural habits as closely as possible using rock outcroppings taken from elsewhere in Colorado. Also popular is Predator Ridge, where animals such as hyenas and lions roam. Meanwhile, Primate Panorama is a great place to check out monkeys swinging from tree branches. Some visitors will also want to time their trips to certain parts of the zoo with feeding times there.
7. Downtown Aquarium
Those who love aquatic animals should ensure that a visit to Downtown Aquarium is on their list of Denver Colorado things to do. It is home to a million gallons of water and thousands of animals, including impressive creatures such as sharks and even Sumatran tigers, which are endangered and which, contrary to the reputation that feline animals have, enjoy swimming. You can also get into the water yourself through its Swim with the Fish and Dive with the Sharks programs.
One of the focuses of this aquarium is on the path that water takes along the Colorado River towards the Pacific Ocean; note that this river normally does not reach ocean water as it usually dries up just prior to reaching the Gulf of California. Another focus is on Indonesia's Kampar River, which empties into the Strait of Malacca, which is connected with the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
8. Denver Museum of Nature & Science
A visit to the Denver Museum of Nature & Science is another of the top things to do in Denver for people who enjoy educating themselves as it is a great resource for those who want to learn more about the natural history of the Centennial State, the world and the universe. One of the best ways to do the latter is to take a visit to its 125-seat Gates Planetarium. Also in the Denver Museum of Nature & Science is a 440-seat Phipps IMAX Theater.
Its exhibits include dinosaur bones dating hundreds of millions of years and Egyptian mummies that are thousands of years old. It also has a wildlife exhibit that provides information on animals that are based throughout the world. Overall, it touches upon anthropology, geology, health sciences, space sciences, paleontology and zoology.
9. Children's Museum of Denver
One of the best Denver attractions to bring kids to is this one. It provides an enjoyable, hands-on approach to learning that has young ones talking about the experience for time to come with its impressive variety of exhibits and fun plays capes. Some of the activities that children can take part in include challenging their minds on computer games, learning about science in laboratories and being a cashier in a play grocery store.

TITLE: FAQ Skydive Castroville- 7 Outstanding answers you need to know.
What is Tandem Skydiving?
First time jumpers are securely harnessed to a certified Tandem Skydive Instructor. Search FAQ Skydive Castroville for more information. You can always call customer service at (830)444-5003 with any questions or concerns.
We provide everything from FAQ and pre-jump instruction, all needed equipment and skydive goggles. allows most people to experience terminal velocity and the sensation of flight under a high performance parachute. To freefall over a mile securely fastened to a -certified instructor is the safest way to experience skydiving today.
What should I wear?
Here are some examples of clothing to wear skydiving: Basically we need comfortable outddor clothing based on the weather of the day. It is always a good idea to bring an extra layer with you just in case.
Pants should be comfortable and washable. You may get dirt on your but…
T-shirts should be good in most situations. We recommend sleeves instead of thin straps.
Tennis Shoes/Sneakers or any soft soled shoes that can be tied tightly, We won’t help you look for them…lol
Please no boots or sandals.
Eat lightly, drink plenty of water. Dramamine is great for motion sickness.
What should I expect?
Skydiving is an extreme sport that requires many factors to be in place to be safe.
It is not uncommon to make more than one attempt at scheduling your jump. Many factors can delay or cancel jumps for the day including weather, airport delays, aircraft maintenance, instructor availability and other factors have delayed skydive operations. Skydiving is an extreme sport, be patient, plan ahead.
How long does Skydiving take?
It generally takes 1-2 hours to complete your first Tandem jump. Most of that time is spent waiting on your aircraft, the actual flight time is about 15 minutes and about 5-7 minutes to descend from the open parachute.Remember to be flexible, plan to check-in for your skydive 15-30 minutes prior to your appointment time. At that time you will be given your actual jump time. In most cases you will be on the aircraft within 30 minutes to an hour after arrival. Please allow 4 hours to complete your skydive. Texas has pretty predictable weather, but unexpected delays are not unusual.
Will my weight affect my jump?
235 lbs. max weight*.
Certain body types less than the max. weight still may not fit safely into the skydive equipment. If you weigh over 200 lbs. you must be at 68 inches tall. If you have concerns please speak with customer service for more information.
*fees may apply, see price page for details.3
How many people can be in the aircraft?
We fly two Tandem passengers at a time in the aircraft.
The two of you and your skydive instructors will fly to altitude in about 15-20 minutes. Enjoy the view and relax.
When does the door open?
The door opens above 12,000′ – Relax!
Your instructor will give you simple instructions and jump with you out the door. Freefall will last about 35-45 seconds at speeds over 125 miles per hour.
Your parachute opens around 5000′.
ou feel the wind stop and peacefully float down from 5000′. Your parachute ride lasts about 5-7 minutes. Groups will be able to view and photograph their friends and family from the skydive spectator area.

TITLE: Skydiving in Hill Country Is a Totally Unique Experience! Find Out Why
Skydiving in Hill Country Is a Totally Unique Experience! Find Out Why
Skydiving Over Hill Country
Have you ever wanted to visit France, but never learned French? Have you ever wanted to if it weren’t for the whole “not having wings” thingIf so, you are in luck! Skydiving over Hill Country Skydive Castroville is rooted in the south of France. Alsatian settled the area a while back and still keep a bit of France.
French country and small-town charm meet in Texas Hill Country. A hidden gem founded in 1844, Castroville is a cozy village outside of San Antonio that we are happy to call home. The rolling scenery of Medina County highlights the pioneer-era and French-inspired architecture. While you enjoy your stay, allow us to show you the view from above our little piece of France — right here in Texas! Lush and vibrant, a spectrum of green lays ready to catch you, inviting you into its arms 12,000ft below.
This green quilt is made up of hundreds of patches that make for an unforgettable sight on your weekend getaway. Each location is rich with beauty and history, and we’d like to share some of our favorites with you. So what are some sights to be seen during your skydiving in hill country experience?
Castroville Poppies
Did you know that ? In flower beds, on riverbanks, and in the wild, millions of poppies blanket our town each year. There are many fabulous ways to view the flowers, and we recommend adding aerial viewing to your itinerary in celebration of these red beauties.
Castroville is the poppy capital of Texas
Poppies can be spotted while skydiving over hill country. when they are at their best and brightest from mid-March to late-April. Their fiery floral faces greet you from below and are a welcome treat against all of the green hills, breaking up their gentle waves with a flash of color.
Medina River
Known by many names but most commonly referred to as the Medina, this river snakes its way through the hills and valleys of Castroville. The feeds into the San Antonio River, as well as into Medina Lake, a reservoir at the base of Medina Dam. It runs through many of our fine recreational facilities, butting right up against Koenig Park as wall as embanking Castroville Regional Park. For generations, the river has energized Castroville with its waters.
When you are above, notice the houses that line its banks. It’s easy to see why early pioneers built their high pitched roofs along its calm banks, including Castroville’s famed Alsatian Steinbach House. Only from the sky can you see the influence the river has had all across the county, along with how it continues to connect the town with surrounding farmland.
Cross Hill
Stemming from European customs brought over with settlers of the area, Cross Hill is a symbol of the faith they brought with them when they came to the Medina Valley. Also known as Mont Gentilz, named after Theodore Gentilz, this is a gentle 1 mile hike located within Castroville Regional Park.
While a peaceful place to rest after a long day, the Cross trail may be lacking in intensity for some. The 13-foot high, 7-foot wide cross that stands on the hill is unfortunately not the original, but an equally magnificent replacement erected in 1902. As you skydiving over hill country, look for the clearing the Cross calls home. If you spot it, marvel at how it peeks from the trees, watching over the town as it has for over a hundred years.
Medina Dam
Touched on above, is located within a popular recreational facility called Paradise Canyon. Paradise Canyon is great place to spend the day with your family, but if you are hoping for a look at the dam you will be sorely disappointed. The dam has not been open to the public for years, and even on the lake, there are strict guidelines about staying no less than 300 feet away at all times. While there are currently efforts to get the dam reopened to the public, at the moment your options are limited.
Fortunately for you, the most exciting way we recommend to view the Medina Dam is in tandem with one of our instructors! Skydiving is one of the few ways to get a glimpse of the historic walkways. It’s also the only way to see the dam’s towering 164-foot walls in action as they hold back all of mighty Medina Lake. Medina Dam is a must-see from the skies, providing the county with irrigation and recreation since 1912.
Skydiving in Hill Country … Is it Worth it?
Where else can you both skydive and then celebrate with delectable French pastries? If you want a true living landscape or to see a little slice of heaven, skydiving in Hill Country Is the way to go. When you climb into the cab of the plane, your heart will be beating in your ears and your stomach may try to jump into your throat – but as you climb higher and higher, take a deep breath and look out at that gorgeous green quilt below. It holds so many possibilities, all of which are within your grasp. You just need to make that jump.
When you dive in and see those clouds rush past you, it’s hard to believe you only have around a minute of free fall. At 5,000ft your chute will deploy and you will experience the magic of flight along with an absolutely breathtaking view.
The glimpses of deer and javelina running through the valley, the twisting and turning of the Medina River, and the curve of the horizon before you never gets old. Whether on your first jump or 80th, you will always find something new when skydiving over hill country. No matter if you’re visiting on a poppy-studded spring day or a hot summer evening, we guarantee you a stunning view and unforgettable memory.
What are you waiting for? skydiving over hill country and treat yourself to a thrill and book today! If you miss anything due to season or simply the excitement of flight, don’t worry. You will always have a seat in our cab!

Why Humpback Whales come to Hawaii
Every winter, one of nature’s greatest migrations unfolds just offshore from Waikiki. Thousands of North Pacific humpback whales travel up to 3,000 miles from Alaska to the warm, shallow waters of Hawaii. They come not to feed – they survive on fat reserves built during summer – but to give birth, nurse their calves, and mate. The result for whale watchers is extraordinary: the whales are relaxed, social, and active near the surface.
During peak season (January and February), it’s common to encounter mothers with newborn calves, competitive pods of males pursuing females, and extended surface activity including full breaches, tail slaps, pec slaps, and spy-hops. Adult humpbacks reach up to 45 feet in length and 40 tons. Seeing one launch its full body out of the ocean – and hearing the thunderous splash that follows – stops guests mid-sentence every single time.

What Is Turtle Canyon?
Turtle Canyon is a shallow reef system just offshore from Waikiki on Oahu’s south shore. It serves as Oahu’s most established natural cleaning station – affectionately known by our crew and locals as a “turtle car wash.” Hawaiian Green Sea Turtles (honu) congregate here specifically because schools of local reef fish love to eat the algae right off their shells. The turtles enjoy this spa-like treatment so much that they reliably stay in the area year-round to get pampered!
On any given morning or afternoon, you’re likely to encounter multiple turtles hovering over the reef for their car wash, surfacing for a breath of air, or resting on the sandy bottom. You may also spot octopus (tako), and an abundance of colorful reef fish.
Turtle Canyon is widely considered the best snorkeling spot in Honolulu, and arguably the best snorkeling on Oahu, for one simple reason: it’s not a boat trip to a random reef hoping to get lucky. The turtles are reliably here waiting for their car wash, and it all sits just minutes offshore from your hotel in Waikiki.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.

Frisco Bay Marina is a premier destination for enjoying and the surrounding Rocky Mountains. Located just steps from downtown Frisco, the marina offers boat rentals, paddle sports, and seasonal slip rentals, making it easy for visitors and locals to get out on the water. With beautiful mountain views and easy access to nearby parks and trails, it’s the perfect place to spend a summer day on the lake.
Getting to the Frisco Bay Marina
The Frisco Bay Marina is located on the shores of Dillon Reservoir in Frisco, Colorado. From Interstate 70, take Exit 203 and head south on Summit Boulevard/Highway 9 toward Frisco. After approximately 0.5 miles, turn left onto Marina Road. Please go to the to find out more about current road conditions.

We know you are excited to get out on the water, but everyone 18 years or older in your group will need to fill out the waiver before heading out on the water. Minors will need to be added by a parent or legal guardian.
Know before you go
Summers in Frisco typically involve blue skies and temps in the 70s or 80s with low humidity. Maybe there will be a brief and refreshing mid-afternoon “sun shower”. In other words, summertime is usually just about as perfect as it gets.
We’re all about adopting a spontaneous sense of adventure here in Frisco. However, if you’re planning on renting a boat or watercraft of any kind, don’t show up without a reservation, or you’ll probably be out of luck.
Also, although we do have a sandy beach here, there’s no lifeguard on duty. And frankly, the best way to enjoy Dillon Reservoir is on top of it. Due to local regulations swimming and water skiing are not permitted on Dillon Reservoir – bummer, we know. The water in this high alpine reservoir is simply too cold for swimming; after all, it was literally snow right before it arrived here.
The Frisco Bay Marina offices also carry snacks and refreshments so you won’t go hungry while on the water.
