Things you should know before Skydiving
WE KNOW you have so many questions, so check below first, then if you still have more, there is always a human at the end of our phone.
Is tandem skydiving safe?
Yes! Tandem skydiving has a , with highly trained instructors and regularly maintained equipment. While all adventure sports carry some risk, drop zones in Canada follow strict regulations for safety.
Do I need any prior experience to do a tandem skydive?
No, tandem skydiving is designed for beginners. You’ll be securely harnessed to a certified tandem instructor who handles everything, from exit to landing. Before your jump, you’ll receive a safety briefing explaining the process.
What are the age and weight requirements for tandem skydiving in Canada?
The minimum age is typically At Skydive Ontario, If you’re under 18 you’ll need parental consent and them on site. Our weight Limit is 240lbs (110Kg) for safety reasons.
How high will I jump from, and how long is freefall?
Most tandem skydives in Canada happen from . Freefall lasts , depending on the altitude, followed by a parachute descent.
How long does the entire skydiving experience take?
Plan for at the drop zone. The jump itself lasts about , including freefall and parachute descent, but check-in, training, and waiting for your flight can take longer, especially on busy days.
What should I wear for my tandem skydive?
Wear and lace-up sneakers. Avoid sandals, boots, or anything loose. In cooler months, bring . The drop zone may provide a jumpsuit to wear over your clothes.
What happens if the weather is bad on the day of my jump?
Skydiving is , and safety is always the priority. If conditions aren’t suitable (strong winds, low clouds, rain, or storms), your jump may be . The drop zone will contact you if there are delays or changes.
Where will my skydive take place?
Skydive Ontario, Cayuga, Ontario.
Can I skydive with friends or as part of a group?
Yes! Skydiving with friends or as a team makes the experience even better. Booking larger groups should be made far in advance to ensure the entire group can jump that day.
Where are my Goggles?!
Don’t panic, your instructor has them.
What does freefall feel like?
It feels more like because of the strong wind resistance. There’s no roller-coaster drop sensation—just a smooth, exhilarating rush.
Can I breathe during freefall?
Yes! The rush of air may feel intense, but you can through your nose and mouth. If you feel short of breath, try yelling—it helps regulate breathing.
What happens if the parachute doesn’t open?
Every tandem skydive includes a . Instructors are trained for emergencies, and modern parachutes are equipped with that deploy the reserve parachute if needed.
What if I’m afraid of heights?
Surprisingly, many people with a fear of heights skydive without issues. The altitude is so high that the ground doesn’t appear close, making it feel less intimidating than standing on a tall building.
Can I change my skydive date after signing up?
Yes, but rescheduling depends on . If you need to change your date, contact us as soon as possible.
Can I bring my own camera or GoPro on the skydive?
No, for safety reasons. Small objects like cameras can become and interfere with your instructor’s equipment. However, professional are available for purchase at the drop zone.

TITLE: FAQs | Lady Caroline
Ticketing & Arrival
Do I have to purchase tickets in advance?
Advance purchase is strongly encouraged, as our cruises often sell out quickly. Tickets can be purchased online or by calling the office directly.
How soon should I book a cruise? Do you need advance notice?
We recommend booking your cruise as soon as possible. Many of our cruises sell out in advance. Friday and Saturday nights during the summer are extraordinarily popular and often reach capacity several weeks in advance.
What is included in the price?
The ticket price includes your boarding pass, a delicious buffet meal, musical entertainment (all cruises feature a DJ), water, coffee, and iced or hot tea. Soft drinks and alcoholic beverages are available for purchase. Tickets do not include tax or gratuity.
How do I purchase tickets?
Reservations can be made by calling 216.696.8888. You may also make your reservation online.
What discounts are available?
Throughout the season, we may send exclusive offers to our LC VIPs. .
Join the list here
Are gift certificates available?
Yes! Gift certificates are available. .
Order them here
How early should I arrive?
Boarding begins one hour prior to the cruise. Guests are encouraged to allow time for parking, check-in and relaxation. It is important that our cruises depart on time.
What time does boarding begin?
Boarding starts one hour prior to the scheduled cruise time.
When is the latest I can get there?
You can board up to 10 minutes prior to our departure time.
What happens if I arrive late?
All cruises depart promptly at the specified time due to our schedule. All guests have been informed of the cruise departure time and should anticipate it to be accurate. It is imperative that guests be aboard at least 10 minutes prior to the cruise departure time to avoid missing the boat!
What if I miss the ship? Do I get a refund?
No refunds are issued within 72 hours of the cruise. We will try to accommodate you on another cruise, based on availability.
What is your cancellation policy?
Cancellations made prior to 72 hours are transferable and refundable. Cancellations made within 72 hours or less may be rescheduled within the same season as purchased but are not refundable. (Not applicable to contracted groups.) All major credit cards accepted. We do not accept personal checks.
What do I need to bring with me the day of?
Please bring your boarding passes (attached to your receipt) and head straight to the boat upon arrival.
Is there a charge for parking? If so, what is it and do they take credit cards?
There is a parking lot connected to Lady Caroline operated by Propark Mobility. Prices are subject to change without notice, but typical rates are $3 – $15. Rates and payment options may vary based on events happening in the area. During Jacobs Pavilion concerts and Nautica Waterfront District special events, parking may be cash only. If the gates are down, take a ticket and pay as you leave. If there is a Propark Mobility team member at the gate, notify them
you are here for a Lady Caroline cruise.
Is there public transportation to Lady Caroline?
RTA does not offer service to our dock at this time. Many of our guests use ride-sharing apps such as Uber and Lyft. If there is NOT a concert at Jacobs Pavilion, ride-share drivers may enter the lot free of charge and pick passengers up in front of the dock. If there is an event, we ask drivers to meet passengers at the end of Main Street – just a short walk down the boardwalk.
How do I get to the dock?
Lady Caroline docks along the Cuyahoga River in Cleveland, Ohio.
Schedule
Do you cruise every day?
During the Summer, we cruise most days. During the Spring, Autumn and Winter our cruising days are more limited.
How late in the season do you cruise?
Our season is dependent on weather, but generally we begin on Easter and run through New Year’s Eve.
How long is the cruise?
Varies by season and time of day.
What is a Holiday or Special Cruise?
These are special celebration voyages themed around traditional holidays (i.e., Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, Cinco de Mayo, Halloween, New Year’s Eve, etc.) or one of the many exciting events happening in Cleveland (i.e., Airshow, Tall Ships, etc.). They are open to the public but often sell out quickly!
Are private tours/charters available?
Yes! Private tours and charters are a great idea for any special event you are planning, from weddings, anniversaries and corporate gatherings to client entertaining or birthday parties. We believe “The Best Events are on the Water!” 100-150 paid fares required.
Will Lady Caroline cruise rain or shine?
Absolutely! Lady Caroline has three fully enclosed, climate-controlled decks for your comfort. In case of severe weather conditions or upon direction of the U.S. Coast Guard or National Weather Service, the boat may remain dockside until weather conditions improve. Please keep in mind that our weather patterns can change quickly (this is Cleveland, afterall.) In the rare event that we are forced to cancel the trip, you will be allowed to reschedule to another time (subject to availability).
How is seating handled? Is it first come, first served?
Seating is preassigned by the restaurant manager. Parties may be seated together. You will be escorted to your reserved seats when you board the ship. If you would like to be seated with another party, please contact the office, 216.696.8888. We do our best to accommodate these requests – but we can’t guarantee it.
Is there air conditioning/heating on board?
Yes, Lady Caroline offers 3 fully-enclosed, climate-controlled decks for your cruising comfort.
Are there life jackets on board?
Yes, Lady Caroline has more than enough life jackets available for all passengers at any time. The Captain’s safety briefing explains where they are located. You are not required to wear life jackets during the cruise.
Is the ship wheelchair accessible?
The ship has limited wheelchair accessibility. We can accommodate manual wheelchairs only—no powered/electric scooters. Please contact 216.696.8888 to discuss.
Are restrooms available?
Yes. Lady Caroline has clean restrooms on each floor.
The Experience
What kind of music does the DJ play? Do you take requests?
Our DJ plays a wide variety of music throughout the cruise. Soft music while you are dining and then typically adult contemporary music after your meal is completed. Requests are welcome.
Is smoking allowed on the boat?
No. Lady Caroline is a smoke/vape-free vessel. We do not allow the smoking of cigarettes, cigars, vape pens or e-cigarettes on any of the decks.
What do you do for birthdays?
Our DJ is always happy to announce your special day. Please speak with our crew when you are on board.
What is the dress code?
Although we do not have a strict dress code, we recommend “Business Casual.”
Will I get seasick?
Lady Caroline is a large and stable boat and the Cuyahoga River and Lake Erie are typically calm waters. As a result, very little motion is felt on board the yacht. Seasickness is very rare. If you are prone to motion sickness, please consider consulting your physician prior to your cruise.
Where does the cruise go?
The route is at the Captain’s discretion and based on weather and river traffic. The route is determined on the day of the cruise. We will either cruise on Lake Erie, stay within the break wall or cruise on the Cuyahoga River.
What else can I do in the area?
We are located in the Nautica Waterfront District in downtown Cleveland. Our dock is home to exciting entertainment venues right on the Cuyahoga River. The possibilities are endless whether you want to grab dinner and drinks, tune in to live music or (in the daytime) get nose-to-nose with sharks.

=== PAGE: https://skydivewindycitychicago.com/faq/
TITLE: FAQ - skydivewindycitychicago.com
Frequently Asked Questions
🪂 Tandem Skydive Experience & Timing
How long will my Tandem Skydive Take?
You should anticipate spending about 3 hours with us for your tandem skydive. There could be delays due to weather that are unforeseen but we do our best to communicate that with you as soon as we possibly can.
Should I eat something before I jump?
ABSOLUTELY!
Please eat a nutritious meal before skydiving. NO ALCOHOL OR DRUGS before making your skydive. Safety is our utmost priority and this could hinder you from making your skydive.
📋 Reservations, Age & Weight Requirements
Do I need a reservation?
We HIGHLY recommend it. While we can occasionally honor walk-ins we CANNOT guarantee we will have room for you, so please make a reservation.
Click here to schedule a reservation
How old do I need to be?
To be able to book and do a tandem skydive, or any type of skydive you must be at least 18 years old. This will be verified by ID on the day of the jump.
Is there a weight restriction?
For the safety of our tandem students and our tandem instructors there is a weight restriction. 250 pounds is the max weight for a tandem skydive. Anyone that is 210-250 pounds will need to pay an additional $40 charge.
👕 What to Wear & Bring
What should I wear?
Wear something that you don’t mind getting a little dirty and dress comfortable. Keep in mind it’s usually a little cooler at altitude than on the ground. Tennis shoes, jeans, sweats, shorts, leggings and if it’s cold, bring an extra layer or two. If you have long hair, wear it up or in a braid if possible.
Open-toed shoes or sandals and lace up boots/heels are NOT allowed due to safety reasons.
💲 Pricing, Discounts & Tipping
Do you offer discounts?
Yes. We offer discounts for active duty military, veterans, students and group discounts starting at groups of 4 people. Please see our page for details.
Should I tip my instructor?
Yes!
While we will never expect a tip we always appreciate them! We have tip boxes set out and logbooks you can sign. We love reading your feedback and comments from the jump!
Do you offer refunds?
Yes, anything paid directly to Skydive Windy City it is 100% refundable.
📸 Photos, Video & Media Packages
Can I wear a GoPro?
You CAN NOT wear your own camera as a tandem jumper. This is a USPA regulation and has to do with safety for both the students and instructors. If you are an experienced skydiver with at least 200 jumps, you can wear your own camera.
I bought a Media Package - how long will it take to receive it?
You will typically receive your media packages within an hour but can take up to 24 hours if we are extremely busy. They are sent to your email so please remember to check your spam folder.
Can multiple people be filmed at the same time?
We CANNOT video more than one person at a time, other than a quick shot in the plane or on the ground. Each person needs to purchase their own media package if they wish to have video/pictures.
♿ Special Accommodations & Accessibility
Do you offer tandems for people with Special Needs?
Yes we do! Please reach out to us directly to inquire about these jumps.
Do you have female Tandem Instructors for religious purposes?
Unfortunately, as of the 2026 season we do not have female tandem instructors.
🍔 On-Site Amenities
Do you have food or drinks on site?
Yes, we have vending machines outside the main building at the pavilion.
🚗 Parking, Transportation & Getting Here
Do you have a place to park?
We have ample parking at our facility. We generally open the gates 30 minutes prior to opening for the day.
Can I take public transportation (train)?
You can take the South Shore Line from the city right to the Michigan City stop. From there it’s just a short Uber ride to our facility.
🐾 Pets & Visitors
Can I bring my pet?
While we love pets, skydiving is not very pet friendly and we kindly ask that you leave your pets at home.
Are kids allowed at the dropzone to spectate?
Yes, as long as they are DIRECTLY supervised by a member of your party.

Vancouver Cruise Tips (FAQ – A Complete Guide)
Welcome to Vancouver Cruise Tips, your ultimate resource for making the most of your cruise adventure departing from the stunning port city of Vancouver. Situated on the pristine west coast of Canada, Vancouver is a captivating blend of urban sophistication and natural beauty. Vancouver: A Cruise Destination Like No Other
Vancouver isn’t merely a city; it’s a world-class port that seamlessly blends cosmopolitan allure with the stunning backdrop of the Pacific Ocean and the Coastal Mountains. Few places offer such a diverse and enchanting prelude to your cruise. The city’s cruise terminals, each with its unique character, welcome travellers from all around the world. From Canada Place with its iconic white sails that have become a symbol of the city to Ballantyne Pier’s historic charm, the start of your cruise experience in Vancouver is nothing short of extraordinary.

These voyages promise adventure, wonder, and a connection to nature that is nothing short of profound.

This guide leaves no stone unturned, covering every aspect of your journey, from planning your cruise to disembarking and exploring Vancouver.

Chapter 1: Pre-Cruise Planning
Choosing Your Cruise
Embarking on a cruise from Vancouver is an exciting opportunity to explore some of the most breathtaking destinations in the world. The first step in your pre-cruise planning is choosing the perfect cruise that aligns with your interests and preferences. Vancouver offers a wide array of cruise options, and each one promises a unique experience.
Vancouver is one of the primary gateways to the pristine wilderness of Alaska. If you’re seeking adventure amid towering glaciers, wildlife sightings, and lush landscapes, an Alaskan cruise is the perfect choice. Cruise lines like Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, and Norwegian Cruise Line offer awe-inspiring journeys to the Last Frontier.
These cruises typically explore the Pacific coastline of North America, offering passengers a blend of cityscapes and natural beauty. Destinations might include Seattle, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. is one of the vessels providing memorable Pacific Coastal cruises.
Vancouver is a major hub for transpacific voyages, often travelling to Asia, Hawaii, or other international destinations. Repositioning cruises occur when ships move between seasons or regions. Keep an eye out for these unique itineraries that may offer longer voyages with different embarkation and disembarkation ports.
When choosing your cruise, it’s essential to select a cruise line that aligns with your expectations for service, entertainment, and amenities. Here are some of the popular cruise lines that operate from Vancouver:
Known for its classic cruising experience, Holland America offers a range of Alaskan cruises from Vancouver. Enjoy elegant dining, cultural enrichment, and comfortable accommodations.

Best Time to Cruise
Summer is the most popular time for cruising from Vancouver. This season offers the warmest and most pleasant weather, making it ideal for exploring destinations like Alaska. The summer months also boast extended daylight hours, giving you more time to soak in the stunning landscapes and wildlife.
If you prefer milder weather and fewer crowds, consider cruising during early fall. The summer rush has subsided, and you’ll still enjoy beautiful scenery and wildlife sightings. The crisp, autumn air adds a touch of magic to your journey.
Springtime cruises provide an opportunity to witness nature’s rebirth. The landscapes come alive with blooming flowers and wildlife emerging from hibernation. While it might be slightly chillier, spring offers a unique and refreshing experience.
Cruising during the late fall and winter months is excellent if you’re interested in saving on fares and don’t mind the cooler weather. While it’s not the peak time for Alaskan cruises, it’s an excellent choice for Pacific Coastal cruises or voyages to warmer destinations.

TITLE: FAQs | Hoover Dam | Boulder City NV | LakeMeadCruises.com
Have questions? Let us help.
How far is Lake Mead from Las Vegas?
Lake Mead is located depending on traffic and your starting point. It’s an easy and scenic trip, making it perfect for a day excursion or private charter experience away from the city hustle.
approximately 30 miles (48 km) from the Las Vegas Strip, which is a roughly 35–45 minute drive,
How far in advance should I book?
The Sightseeing cruise does not typically sell out completely, so if your last-minute plans include visiting Lake Mead, you should book on our website when you’ve solidified your plans. We take bookings right up to 30 minutes prior to departure. When meal cruises are operating, we recommend booking at least 1 week prior.
How large is the parking lot?
Our parking lot is a dirt parking lot on the beach. There is no parking fee, just the entrance fee payable to the National Park Service. It is about the size of a football field.
Is there bus parking?
Yes, but it is not marked. Upon arrival, staff can assist with where to park if there are any questions.
Are there restrooms at the landing before boarding the vessel? How large are they?
Yes, we have an accessible restroom plus six gender-neutral restrooms before boarding the boat. There are also restrooms on the boat – an accessible restroom plus two general-neutral ones on the first deck and two more gender-neutral restrooms on the second deck.
Are pets allowed?
Only service animals are allowed.
What are the ADA accommodations?
Vehicles can pull up to the front of the head and walk to drop someone off. The 1st deck and restrooms are ADA-accessible. Scooters and wheelchairs can take the path to the boat and board. We also have a wheelchair to assist with boarding.
Can I book a live band to play music on the boat?
Yes if you are also booking a private charter, but not if you are joining a public cruise.
Can I bring my own alcohol for my party?
No, no outside food or beverage is not allowed, except for water.
What items are not allowed to bring?
Weapons, marijuana, drones, metal detectors, and wrapped gifts (gift bag only). Bags are subject to search prior to boarding as per Homeland Security regulations.
How far are you from the Hoover Dam?
15 minutes by car.

FAQ
Answers to the questions we get asked the most.
How much is a jet ski rental in Miami?
Jet ski rentals in Miami range from $50 to $150 per hour depending on duration. We offer package deals for 2+ hours with significant savings. All rentals include life jackets, safety gear, and a comprehensive safety briefing.
How much does it cost to rent an ATV in Miami?
ATV rentals start at $150 for a 2-hour guided tour. Price includes helmet, safety gear, and a professional guide. Group discounts available for parties of 4 or more.
Do I need a license to rent a jet ski in Florida?
Anyone born on or after January 1, 1988 needs a Florida Boating Safety Education ID Card. You can get a temporary certificate online at boattests101.com in about 30 minutes. We'll help you through the process!
Where can I take the test for my boating certificate?
You can take the test online through boattests101.com
Take the Test →
What is the minimum age to drive a jet ski in Miami?
Florida state law requires jet ski renters to be 18 or older with a valid photo ID (Florida Statute 327.395). Once rented, operators must be 14+ and need a Boating Safety Education ID if born on or after January 1, 1988. We provide the safety briefing before every ride.
What is the minimum age to ride as a passenger?
Children 6 years and older can ride as passengers with an adult driver. Life jackets are provided in all sizes for kids.
Where are the best places to jet ski in Miami?
The best spots include Biscayne Bay with stunning Miami skyline views, Haulover Sandbar for celebrity homes and island hopping, and the open Atlantic for high-speed free riding. Our guides know all the secret spots!
Is there a security deposit required?
No security deposit required! We only require 30% of the total amount when booking online. The remaining balance is paid at check-in.
What is your cancellation policy?
Full refund with 24+ hours notice. No refund for no-shows or cancellations under 24 hours. Weather cancellations by us always receive full refund or reschedule.
What happens if it rains on my jet ski rental day?
Light rain doesn't stop the fun. Jet skiing in the rain is actually a blast! However, if there's lightning, high winds, or unsafe conditions, we'll reschedule your ride for free or offer a full refund. Safety always comes first.
Do I need experience to ride a jet ski in Miami?
No prior experience is needed! Our team provides a full safety briefing and riding instructions before every rental. Jet skis are easy to operate. If you can ride a bicycle, you can ride a jet ski. We're always nearby if you need help on the water.
What should I bring for a jet ski rental in Miami?
Bring a valid photo ID, sunscreen (reef-safe preferred), sunglasses with a strap, and clothes you don't mind getting wet. We provide life jackets and all safety equipment. Leave valuables in your car. We have limited dry storage.
Can I book jet skis for a group or party in Miami?
Yes. We handle bachelor parties, birthdays, corporate outings, and family groups regularly. If you have more than 4 riders, call us at (786) 553-7644 so we can reserve enough machines. We can also combine jet ski rentals with a boat for larger groups.
What are your hours? When is Funwaves open?
We are open 7 days a week from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The last jet ski rental slot goes out at 4:00 PM. We recommend booking the first slot of the day if you want calm water and fewer boats on the bay.
How much time do I actually spend on the jet ski?
On the 1-hour rental, you get about 50 minutes of riding time after the 5-minute safety briefing and boarding. The 2-hour guided tour gives you the full time on the water since the briefing happens on the escort boat before you start. Check-in is 15 minutes before your slot.

Lake Berryessa is one of California’s largest bodies of fresh water, and with over 165 miles of shoreline, Lake Berryessa offers year-round recreation opportunities for the whole family. Nestled between Blue Ridge and Cedar Roughs, and just east of the Napa Valley, Lake Berryessa is a popular recreation destination for over 1.5 million visitors each year. Summer water temperatures reach 75 degrees, making Berryessa the perfect destination for water sports. The lake is also a popular fishing location for both cold and warm water species. Pleasure Cove Marina operates from the south end of the lake just off highway 128. With an assortment of activities that the lake and surrounding area has to offer, you’ll find exactly what you’re looking for at Pleasure Cove Marina on Lake Berryessa. 1. Is skydiving safe?
Skydiving statistics have proven that tandem skydiving is a safe activity. In fact, relative to other recreational activities that are often perceived as safe, skydiving has a significantly lower incident rate. Skydive Santa Cruz has a perfect safety record.
Skydive Santa Cruz is informing you that skydiving, parachuting, and flying are inherently dangerous activities, which may result in serious injury or even death. All passengers need to be willing and able to accept these risks.
The skydiving industry has dedicated significant resources to mitigate the risk through the innovation of safety equipment and devices, increased proficiency requirements, and rigorous training standards. So, what can you expect from us to mitigate the risk and ensure safe skydiving operations?
Skydiving is regulated in the United States by the United States Parachute Association (USPA) and the Federal Aviation Authority (FAA). Skydive Instructors must meet and adhere to strict regulations set forth by the USPA, including possessing a minimum of 500 skydives and successful completion of a Tandem Instructor Rating course. Our instructors have completed, on average, more than 7000 skydives each.
Our pilots, aircraft operations, and aircraft maintenance must pass the standards by the FAA, the same association that governs major commercial airlines such as Delta, United, and Alaska.
Our tandem skydiving is serviced and maintained by FAA certified parachute riggers. In accordance with FAA and USPA guidelines, our reserve parachutes are inspected and repacked every 180 days. The main parachutes are packed by trained skydiving professionals under a rigger’s supervision. Each of our packers have packed well over 5,000 parachutes each.
We purchase brand new gear from the manufacturer, and swap out aging equipment. Our parachute gear is amongst the top of line within the skydiving industry.
We have implemented our own additional safety procedures above and beyond the requirements set forth by the USPA and FAA. This has been a key component to maintaining a perfect safety record. We will only fly in safe skydiving conditions. You may not be pleased at the time as that could mean your skydive has to be delayed or rescheduled. However, when safety is concerned it trumps your needs, wants, or requests.
2. What if the parachute doesn't open?
Through modern parachute design, parachute packing testing, and experienced parachute packers, the probability of the main parachute not opening is quite low. Parachutes are designed for soft, on-heading, repeatable openings. Statistically speaking less than 0.1% of main parachutes experience opening inconveniences or issues that require corrective action.
Though main parachute opening issues are extremely rare, every tandem skydiving rig is equipped with both a main parachute, a reserve parachute, and an Automatic Activation Device (AAD). Reserve parachutes are packed exclusively by specially trained and FAA certified parachute riggers. The method and the design of the reserve parachute is designed with the primary feature of reliable openings. Reserve parachutes are also inspected every 180 days by Parachute Riggers. Every tandem skydiving system also has an on-board computer that is detects atmospheric conditions (altitude and vertical speed). AADs are programmed to fire the reserve parachute at prescribed altitudes as a redundant back-up safety protocol.
And of course, you’ll be attached to a professional tandem skydive instructor with thousands of skydives of experience. Instructors have been practicing emergency procedures since their first skydives. They have experience, and have successfully, managed unusual and emergency situations.
3. How long does a skydive last?
Your total (although weather or operational issues could further delay that timeframe). That includes check-in, registration, training, gear-up, airplane flight, freefall, and parachute descent.
A tandem skydive requires minimal training as you’ll be paired with an extremely experienced, USPA certified tandem instructor. We will review aircraft safety, aircraft exit procedure, freefall body position, and landing technique. The training and your harness fitting typically require about 10-15 minutes.
We have a fleet of extremely well-maintained aircraft. They are small, personal aircraft commonly used in skydiving operations. On board, it will typically only be the pilot, you and your tandem instructor, and another tandem skydive pair.
The flight up will be a smooth, comfortable, and visually stunning 20-minute flight to jump altitude. We typically fly over the Santa Cruz beaches and Santa Cruz (unless weather or air traffic dictate otherwise). The flight itself is an awesome experience.
Freefall lasts up to 45 seconds at Skydive Santa Cruz. The length of freefall depends upon the exit altitude, parachute opening altitude, and the body weight, body position and surface area of the tandem pair. At Skydive Santa Cruz, we jump between 10,000-12,000 feet (depending on conditions and air traffic) which generally translates into 35-45 seconds of blissful freefall.
Your tandem skydive instructor will deploy the parachute at approximately 5000 feet above the ground. Parachute descent times vary depending upon the flying style (fast turns or slow chill descent), and the amount of suspended weight under the parachute (heavier pairs will descent faster). Parachute descents last between 3-8 minutes.
4. What does freefall feel like?
Explaining the feeling(s) of freefall is a difficult task. Even though all of the individual sensations are incredible, together as a sum, they transform into an indescribable experience. Some of the feelings and sensations you’ll experience during freefall include:
The most out of this world feeling of freefall is weightlessness. It is a feeling of floating on an invisible column. It is like gravity has been suspended. It is close to what astronauts feel in zero gravity.
It’s highly likely you’ve never felt weightlessness before. Sometimes people attach the term weightlessness to the feeling of a rapid and/or dramatic change in direction (e.g., you go over a hill in car rapidly or during the change of direction on a roller coaster). There may be a split-second feeling of weightlessness but the forceful return to the new direction of travel leaves a heavy feeling which is the opposite of freefall weightlessness.
Typically, a tandem skydive pair will freefall at an average speed of 120 mph. So, it’s going be windy and there will be some resistance from the air but nothing to the extent that it restricts motion. You’ve likely felt this before when placing your arm outside of a moving vehicle. You feel the wind push on your body but not to the extent that you can’t control where your arm goes.
Adrenaline rush would be the most used term to describe this physiological sensation. For most people, this starts kicking in prior to freefall. Skydiving activates the fight or flight mechanism in the brain, and in return, the brain sends out a variety of feel-good neurochemicals to help aid you through the experience. One of those chemicals is dopamine which is the brain’s universal reward currency. This is one reason why you’ll feel happy, powerful, confident, alert, and focused during and after your skydive.
Freefall is truly a feeling you’ve never experienced before so trying to compare it something you understand is going to provide a false comparison.
You will not feel like you’re falling. A relative object, or one coming toward you, is required to process the feeling of falling, or speed in general. The ground does not any appear closer from 10,000 feet compared to 8000 feet above ground, yet you’ve fallen at 120mph for 10 seconds. By the time you get that close to the ground you’ve already been flying underneath the parachute for a couple of minutes.

TITLE: Comparing Indoor Skydiving vs Skydiving I Skydive Santa Cruz
Indoor Skydiving Experience Key Takeaways:
Indoor skydiving provides a controlled experience that mimics the sensation of freefall, letting you hover and float in an enclosed vertical wind tunnel.
While less expensive than
real skydiving
, indoor skydiving covers only the freefall portion: no altitude,

, or parachute flight are included.

Individual flights typically last 30 to 60 seconds, with packages often including multiple flights for fun.
Indoor skydiving is used by experienced skydivers to practice body positions, maintain muscle memory, or try new maneuvers in an environment that allows multiple repetitions in a short time span.
Wind tunnels operate in all weather, day or night, providing a convenient way to experience flying sensations.
Indoor skydiving is highly managed, but minor injuries can happen and there are risks, but it is generally regarded as a very safe activity.
Indoor skydiving has been popping up across the country, offering a tempting approximation of what it might feel like to defy gravity without actually leaving the ground. But let us be absolutely clear, “indoor skydiving” is most certainly not skydiving.
Skydiving is the act of exiting from an aircraft while in motion at altitudes typically ranging from 4000-18000 feet above the ground, performing acrobatic maneuvers in freefall, and then landing gracefully, or at least semi-gracefully, by parachute. Indoor skydiving, on the other hand, is what happens when engineers and a strong breeze conspire to let you hover in a vertical wind tunnel while wearing a helmet that makes you look like an off-duty Power Ranger waiting for the call.
Indoor skydiving has no plane, no real freefall, and no parachute landing. It lacks all three critical ingredients that make skydiving…well, skydiving. It’s like calling karaoke a rock concert.
That said, it is fun. It is unique. It is the sort of thing that makes expert skydivers nod approvingly while thinking, “yes, this will make me slightly better at throwing myself out of a plane on future jumps”. It is, to be very clear, a simulation. It is a freefall simulation, which is thrilling in its own confined, tunnel-ish way.
Tunnel flying is a thrilling way to simulate freefall, but can it really compete with jumping out of a perfectly good airplane over the Pacific, flying through the sky toward the ocean at a speed that makes your brain reconsider your life choices. That is exactly where true adventure begins.
The debate, as one might imagine, is not entirely fair.
What is Indoor Skydiving?
At its core, an indoor skydiving experience is a simulated freefall activity within a vertical wind tunnel. Yes, a tunnel. Not a plane, not a vast expanse of open sky overlooking Californian beaches. Just a very determined column of air, contained within a circular tube roughly 12 to 18 feet across, within an enclosed chamber that smells faintly of ambition and overpriced helmet hair.
Some larger wind tunnels reach a height of up to 50 feet. First time flyers only rise a few feet above the metal safety net, which keeps you from falling onto airfoil shaped equipment that aids in the recirculation of airflow. That’s comforting to know when you are questioning how well your Superman impersonation is going. Air is pushed upward at a Category 1 rated hurricane, enough to hold your body aloft so you can hover, float and turn. Fundamentally, it remains an air bound approximation of the real thing.
Why Real Skydiving Beats Indoor Skydiving
Outdoor skydiving is the real deal. It’s the full cinematic experience that wind tunnels can only dream of replicating. It begins with the airplane ride, an odd mixture of anticipation, nervous energy, and the faint hum of engines conspiring to remind you that gravity is waiting.
At Skydive Santa Cruz, that means ocean views that could make even the most jaded travel influencer pause mid-selfie. The coastline stretches out like a living postcard, with crashing waves, towering dunes, the smell of salty air, and a cool breeze against your face.
You can feel the wind speed, orientation changes, the pure freedom of moving through space in a way that no indoor skydiving wind tunnel can hope to reproduce. On a first tandem jump, flips and maneuvers are possible and encouraged.
It is a full-body, sensory thrill. Temperature shifts, the smell of the ocean, the sensation of true altitude. A skydiving experience is a story that will stick with you, not a neatly contained simulation. Nobody makes movies about tunnel flying, but movies are made about people hurling themselves from planes because there is nothing quite like it.
True skydiving delivers speed, altitude, and accomplishment all at once. First-timers and seasoned jumpers leave with the sense of having done something remarkable. A tandem jump is more than just an activity; it is a bucket-list moment, a memory that will live in your heart and mind long after you touch down after parachute descent.
In short, skydiving is not just the real thing, it is the thing you never forget, the thing that changes your perspective, and the thing that makes indoor tunnels feel, well, lacking that je ne sais quoi.
Indoor Skydiving Benefits
Wind tunnel flying has its place, mostly when jumping out of a plane is, for one reason or another, not an option. The indoor skydiving experience is weather-proof, sometimes open at night, and typically available to younger individuals.
For beginners, kids, or anyone nervous about heights, it provides a taste of flying that is manageable and enjoyable. It is a gateway of sorts as an introduction to the motions, the sensation, and the vibes of pretending for a few moments that you’ve unlocked the superpower of flight.
It is a convenient training tool for expert skydivers who want to practice body positions and basic maneuvers without limits of daylight, parachute packing, and weather holds.
Yet, for its merits, indoor skydiving remains fundamentally limited. A contained approximation. A clever illusion. It gives only a hint of freefall, a shadow of true flight, and none of the scale, emotion, or perspective that comes with bailing out of an airplane door with just mental fortitude and sophisticated nylon. Think of it as the skydive appetizer: fun, contained, and worth trying, but the main course is still waiting thousands of feet above the ocean.
Indoor Skydiving Safety vs Skydiving Safety
Short answer: both are safe. People often assume indoor skydiving is guaranteed safety incarnate and outdoor skydiving is a reckless freefall into the void. The reality is more boring and more comforting. Both activities have risks. Both have safety systems and trained staff. Both see injuries only rarely, and injuries to first timers are even rarer. But they are not apples to apples, because the tunnel only stands in for the freefall portion of a jump while an actual skydive includes aircraft time, freefall, parachute flight and landing.
Is Indoor Skydiving Safer Than Skydiving?
Both indoor and outdoor skydiving are, to the mild disappointment of daredevils everywhere, very safe. For tandem students, skydiving is one of the safest adventure sports, with incident rates so low one National Library of Medicine study calls the risk ‘overstated’.
In the United States, skydiving has the United States Parachute Association (USPA), a national body that diligently collects and publishes safety data every year. Skydive Santa Cruz is a member organization of the USPA. Indoor vertical wind tunnels, on the other hand, have no central governing body. Becoming a licensed skydiver might sound like an insurmountable goal but it’s definitely within reach! SkyDance utilizes the training method provided by the United States Parachute Association (USPA) called “Accelerated Free Fall” or AFF for short.
The AFF training program begins with a 4-6 hour First Jump Course followed by 7 Instructor jumps covering individual learning categories. Each category is designed to build your skills and prepare you to become a solo skydiver.
Throughout the course you will be responsible for deploying your parachute and navigating it to the ground. Once all categories have been completed successfully you’ll be cleared to become a solo skydiver! We have recently invested over $100,000 in new student and tandem parachute equipment to ensure you’ll be jumping equipment that is modern, safe, and well fitted!
Your journey doesn’t end once you achieve solo status. SkyDance has an extensive Coaching program to help you finish the requirements needed to obtain your USPA license. Independently operating USPA rated Coaches will help guide you through the path to obtaining your first license, becoming a safe skydiver and what to expect once you’ve graduated from being a student.
Our goal at SkyDance SkyDiving is to create competent, safe skydivers while still promoting a fun culture. The learning doesn’t stop once you become a licensed skydiver, we pride ourselves in incorporating newly licensed skydivers in all dropzone activities and providing other tools to ensure the learning never stops.
Started AFF already? Just because you haven’t jumped with us before doesn’t mean you can’t start now. You can continue your progression at SkyDance no matter where you started your training. TITLE: Experienced HALO Skydiving - SkyDance SkyDiving
Experienced
HALO Skydiving
If you are an experienced skydiver looking to take your jumping higher, look no further. SkyDance SkyDiving offers HALO training and jumps for the first time and repeat HALO skydivers. HALO jumps are truly spectacular. The combination of extended freefall, special equipment, and extreme exposure to the elements offers an unforgettable experience that is both challenging and rewarding.
SkyDance SkyDiving offers a 3-4 day HALO course twice a year, typically in the spring and fall. The class involves a review of the physiology of HALO jumping as well as familiarization and fitting of special O2 equipment. This is followed by two practice jumps from 13,000’ while using the HALO equipment and techniques. The practice jumps are required for all HALO participants, experienced and novice. Then early on the following mornings, loads will be flown up to 28,000-30,000’ AMSL! While the class takes 2-3 days, we generally schedule a 4 day block in case of weather.
You must meet the following prerequisites to sign up for an Experienced HALO skydive:
Hold a valid USPA C license or foreign equivalent.
Hold a valid FAA class 3 medical certificate or equivalent.
Have no facial hair other than a mustache in order for the oxygen mask to properly seal.
Have an airworthy, safe rig with an AAD installed.
SkyDance SkyDiving will provide all specialized HALO equipment including O2, mask, helmet, goggles, altimeter, and balaclava. You must provide your own parachute system (see above) warm clothing, closed shoes/boots, jumpsuit, and gloves.
Please Read our page for additional information.
Our next HALO jumps will be in October 2024 or May 2025. Sign up for the HALO Mailing List to be the first to be notified when we have firm dates available!
The Experienced HALO Jump Course costs $1300. The 2-3 day course cost includes 2 practice jumps, one HALO jump, specialty equipment rental, & T-shirt.
Reservations will be available when dates are available, are required, and must be paid in full ahead of time. Your reservation can be transferred to another jumper to take your place in this specific event but is not refundable in any way and cannot be credited for future use. Quite simply, this event has limited slots, and high upfront costs to organize. A non-refundable $500 deposit will be required at booking.
The jumping portion of the course takes 2 days, however we have scheduled for a 4 day event in case of weather. Please do not sign up for the course unless you will personally commit to being available during this 4 day period. Not everyone will jump on the same day. We do not guarantee your jump day. Tandems will have priority. We have had jumpers in the past opt to work remotely at the dropzone during the downtimes of their course.

Although we do not require a Tandem Skydive for your first jump we do recommend it. A Tandem Skydive can serve as a good base and learning tool to understand the principles of freefall, canopy control, and landing!

Yes, we are able to accommodate many physical disabilities through the use of adaptive equipment and techniques. Please contact us with any questions specific to your condition. We are able to accommodate a wider range of disabilities on a tandem skydive.

TITLE: Chicago Boat Tours - Sightseeing Boat Tours | Chicago Line Cruises
Sunday Jazz Cruise
In partnership with the Jazz Institute of Chicago, Chicago Line Cruises invites you aboard for an unforgettable evening of live jazz on the Chicago River.
On the last Sunday of July, August, and September, enjoy performances by outstanding local jazz musicians as you cruise through the heart of downtown. Sip a drink from our full-service bar, relax on the open-air decks, and take in the city’s iconic architecture as the soundtrack of Chicago comes to life.
Whether you’re a lifelong jazz enthusiast or simply looking for a unique summer evening, this intimate cruise offers the perfect blend of music, scenery, and Chicago history.
July 26 | August 30 | September 27 Cruise Time: 5:30 to 7:00 pm Tickets: $65
About the Jazz Institute of Chicago
Jazz Institute of Chicago’s mission is to nurture and promote jazz in all its forms.
JIC seeks to keep jazz music thriving and expanding by celebrating the work of musicians past, shining a light on musicians present, and making the way brighter for musicians of the future.
This is realized through community and education programs, 90% of which are free.
Jazz Institute of Chicago’s pillars include • provide jazz education • preserve the legacy of jazz • develop & support Chicago musicians • build Chicago’s jazz community • foster a thriving Chicago jazz scene.

=== PAGE: https://parachutevoltige.com/fr/foire-aux-questions/
TITLE: Des questions à propos de Voltige? Consultez notre FAQ
Combien de temps à l’avance dois-je réserver ?
Pour profiter pleinement de nos créneaux horaires, nous vous encourageons à réserver à l’avance, idéalement 3 semaines à l’avance, afin de garantir vos places. Nous accueillons des arrivées à partir de 8h du matin jusqu’à 17h, et parfois jusqu’à 18h lorsque le soleil se couche plus tard pendant la saison.
Cependant, si votre emploi du temps est plus flexible ou imprévisible, n’oubliez pas que des réservations de dernière minute sont également possibles, en fonction des disponibilités restantes. N’hésitez pas à nous appeler pour obtenir des informations à jour. Ne laissez pas passer cette occasion, que ce soit pour planifier à l’avance ou pour profiter de la spontanéité !
*Concernant la météo, ne vous fiez pas toujours aux prévisions annoncées, car elles peuvent être inexactes. Le jour de votre saut, juste avant de partir de chez vous, nous vous demanderons de nous appeler pour confirmer les conditions météorologiques au moment de votre saut. Si la météo n’est pas favorable, nous reprogrammerons votre saut à une autre date en fonction de vos disponibilités.
Recevez une carte-cadeau virtuelle à imprimer instantanément ( moins de 5 minutes) après votre achat en linge. Nous vous invitons à vérifier vos courriers indésirables si non reçu.
Par la poste : délai de 3 à 4 jours ouvrables
Quelle est la limite de poids pour faire un saut tandem?
La limite de poids est de 250 livres (113 kilos). Pour toute personne excédant 230 livres(104 kilos). vous serez évalué et des frais de 50$ s’appliqueront sur le saut.
Puis-je faire filmer mon saut ?
3 options s’offrent à vous
Option A: Photos selfie sous-voilure | 85$+tx Option B: Vidéo + photos filmé par un caméraman externe en chute libre | 145$+tx Option C: (l’option A + B jumelée) | 195$+tx
Voir lien pour plus d’informations :
parachutevoltige.com/…em/coffret-souvenir
Dois-je donner un pourboire à mon instructeur/ instructrice
Nous souhaitons rappeler à nos aimables clients que les pourboires sont à votre discrétion mais toujours appréciés. Nous vous remercions par avance pour cette attention.
Il est essentiel de prévoir la formation théorique, généralement dispensée les dimanches matin. Ensuite, planifiez une soirée à la soufflerie intérieure (Skyventure) à Laval, habituellement le mercredi suivant votre formation théorique. Nous recommandons de ne pas étirer la formation sur plusieurs jours afin d’optimiser vos sauts le plus rapproché possible pour une meilleure expérience et performance.
En ce qui concerne les sauts, s’il fait beau, il est possible de réaliser les 9 sauts en 3 ou 4 jours. Si vous résidez en région, voici différentes options d’hébergement :
Hébergements : Une diversité d’options est disponible dans la région de Lanaudière, notamment à Berthierville avec le Day’In, à Joliette avec le Château Joliette, et à proximité de Parachute Voltige, l’Auberge ma Maison à Sainte-Mélanie. Nous avons également des Campings a proximité de Voltige dont le Camping Nadeau et Camping Paradis.
Voici le lien vers notre programme :
Saut avec Guillaume
Pour effectuer un saut en tandem en compagnie de Guillaume Lemay-Thivierge, celui-ci étant grandement sollicité, nous avons créé une liste d’attente afin de permettre à toutes les personnes de réaliser leur rêve.
Nous vous invitons à communiquer avec nous par téléphone, du lundi au vendredi entre 9h et 16h, pour que nous puissions vous expliquer la procédure et vous y inscrire.
Au plaisir de vous parler.
Est-ce qu’il y a des sauts en hiver
Il n’y a pas de saut durant la saison hivernale . La période de saut est fin avril jusqu’à la mi-octobre.
Météo
Le jour de votre réservation, veuillez nous téléphoner avant de partir de votre domicile afin de vérifier auprès de nous si la température nous permet d’effectuer les sauts pour la journée. Dans le cas où la journée serait annulée, par cause de mauvaise température, le saut sera remis ultérieurement selon votre horaire et nos disponibilités.
Vous pouvez sauter à 9 000 pieds (2 700 mètres) mais à cette altitude, vous ne pourrez pas expérimenter l’expérience optimale de la chute libre puisque l’instructeur déploiera le parachute quelque seconde après la sortie de l’avion.
Le saut le plus populaire, effectué à 13 500 pieds (4 200 mètres), vous permettra de vivre une chute libre de près d’une minute. C’est l’option coup cœur chez Voltige ainsi que dans les plus grandes écoles au monde.
Avec l’option à 18 000 pieds (5 400 mètres) vous passerez environ 1 minute 20 secondes en chute libre. Cette option est souvent choisie par les personnes ayant déjà fait un saut en parachute et qui souhaitent répéter l’expérience, avec un petit extra; de l’oxygène à bord de l’avion et encore plus de chute libre!
Y-a-t-il une limite d’âge?
L’âge recommandé est de 14 ans avec l’autorisation des deux parents. À partir de 16 ans, l’autorisation d’un seul parent est requise. Assurez-vous de remplir le formulaire de consentement parental avant le saut.
Il n’y a pas d’âge maximum. Nous avons eu le plaisir d’accueillir des participants de plus de 100 ans !
Si cela est possible pour vous, nous vous conseillons des lentilles souples. Dans le cas contraire, des lunettes vous serons prêtées pour mettre par dessus vos lunettes de vue.
Comment dois-je m’habiller pour le saut ?
Des vêtements confortables sont préférables. Habillez vous selon les conditions météo du jour. Une combinaison de saut vous sera prêtée.
Qu’arrivera-t-il si notre parachute ne s’ouvre pas ?
Dans la situation où la voilure principale ne fonctionnait pas adéquatement, l’équipement tandem est pourvu d’un deuxième parachute plié de façon très rigoureuse et approuvé par le sceau d’un spécialiste; notre maître gréeur. La formation tandem est donnée par le manufacturier et inclus tous les protocoles d’action en cas de situation inhabituelle. Votre maître tandem doit se soumettre à une formation continue obligatoire à chaque an et est paré à réagir adéquatement à toutes situations.
Que vais-je ressentir en chute libre ?
La sensation en chute libre est beaucoup plus proche du vol que de la chute. Une fois le parachute déployé, tout est calme et merveilleux. Vous ne serez pas limité à un petit hublot et aucun bruit de moteur ne viendra vous distraire. Vous aurez droit à un point de vue privilégié… à vous en couper le souffle.
Le passager est attaché au maître tandem par l’intermédiaire d’un harnais, approuvé pour une charge de plus 5000 lbs.Ce harnais est relié à celui de l’instructeur à quatre endroits par des mousquetons spécialement conçus à cet effet pouvant supporter 2500 lbs chacun.
Votre instructeur vous signalera l’ouverture éminente du parachute par une tape légère sur votre épaule. Vous sentirez alors une transition de état de chute vers une position verticale, suspendue sous la voilure déployée. Les parachutes utilisés pour les sauts en tandem ont été spécialement conçus pour des ouvertures douces et confortables.
Nous utilisons des parachutes rectangulaires, de marque Sigma, qui offrent la meilleure fiabilité sur le marché. La performance et la maniabilité de ces parachutes permettent des atterrissages très précis.
Des équipements à la fine pointe de la technologie.

Our commitment
Tiki Pub is committed to making our website accessible and enjoyable to use for as many people as possible, including people with disabilities. We design and build with inclusivity in mind and continually invest in improvements as standards, tools, and best practices evolve.

A link appears at the top of every page when you press the key, allowing keyboard users to bypass site navigation. Your accessibility preferences are saved on your device and applied automatically to every page you visit.
How we design and build
Throughout the design and development of our website, we follow established accessibility best practices, including those described in the . In practice, this includes:
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1
Semantic HTML structure with logical heading order on every page
Descriptive alternative text on images that convey information
Full keyboard navigation across interactive elements
Color choices reviewed for contrast on body text and primary calls to action
Automatic respect for your operating system's preference
Forms with associated labels and clear, plain-language error messages
A responsive design that works across phones, tablets, and desktops
Regular review and improvement as part of our normal development process
Third-party services
Some functionality on tikipub.com is provided through trusted partner services, including booking and waiver platforms. We choose partners with a strong commitment to accessibility, but the experience within their services is governed by their own standards and practices.

=== PAGE: https://www.plantationadventurecenter.com/crystal-river-florida-manatees
TITLE: Crystal River Florida Manatees | Manatees | Plantation On Crystal River Adventure Center
Manatees
Crystal River Adventures
With guided tours taking off from right behind the Adventure Center, you can take a unique opportunity to swim with the majestic Crystal River, Florida manatees and - with proper precautions taken for their safety - practice passive observance, which helps you come face-to-face (or face-to-snout) with these one-of-a-kind marine mammals!
Book a Manatee Tour
The Experience
About
As part of these Crystal River adventures, we provide detailed pre-tour education and instruction in our full-service facility, as well as snorkels and wetsuits for your use in the water. From there, our captains will take you out onto Kings Bay by boat and guide you through passive observance in the water as soon as a manatee is spotted!
To Expect
What
During this exciting eco-adventure, you can come across 40-50 manatees that stay in the water year-round. However, during the winter months - particularly in November and December, when waters elsewhere become colder - you’ll find hundreds of manatees migrating to the springs, which are at a constant temperature flow of 72°F.
Cruise Tours and Offers
Our cruises are the perfect way to experience Florida's Nature Coast without getting in the water. Opt into one of these special tours and see some local wildlife with picturesque views out on the water. Plus, save on a one-of-a-kind experience in adventure when you book one of our special offers.
Available daily, approximately 60 minutes
The scenic cruise is our one-hour dry tour of Kings Bay. Cruise through the bay with the captain as your guide while you keep your eye out for wildlife and highlights of the area. In addition to manatees, you can take your chance at seeing dolphins, otters, turtles, and a wide variety of birds and fish. Every tour is unique!
Sunset Cruise
Kings Bay
Available on weekends, (Fridays & Saturdays)
approximately 100 minutes
At just over an hour and a half, this guided tour gives you a special glimpse at Florida’s unique wildlife, culminating in an evening sunset that you can enjoy out on the water. While you enjoy a memorable trip through the Nature Coast’s most vibrant habitats, you also have the option to bring drinks and snacks aboard!
Spring Weekday Tours Offer
We’ll let you in on a secret: Adventure Center tours are even better during the week! With fewer crowds around, you'll have more time to swim with the manatees on your own. And to make sure you don’t miss out, we’re offering 20% off weekday tours (Monday - Thursday) when you book with promo code MidWeekMANA through December 31, 2023.
Makes Us Unique
We set ourselves apart from other manatee tours in the area, providing 5mm wetsuits that give additional warmth, buoyancy, and comfort for your tour. This allows you to stay in the water longer and with greater ease! Our tours also include free parking (for non-guests), towels, hot chocolate on the boat, and a shower in the dive shop for you to use after returning.
Q&A
What is the best time to go on a tour?
The best time is early in the morning before Kings Bay gets crowded as well as during the colder periods between late Fall (November and December) and winter (January through March). Weekends tend to get crowded so weekdays tend to be the most opportune time.
What time do you arrive for manatee tours?
Tour times vary. Call Adventure Center for details at and remember that reservations are required.
352-795-5797
How many people do you take out?
Our USCG-certified tour boats accommodate 11 to 14 people per vessel. With the use of all our tour boats, we accommodate groups of up to 48 people. Private tours can also be arranged.
What is the dive experience like?
The Rainbow River (in Dunnellon, 20 miles from our location) is a beautiful location and offers a variety and abundance of freshwater gar, bass, brim, and turtles. The bottom is sand, lime rock, and ribbon grass. It is a drift dive with a relaxing 1.5 to 2 knot current. It’s like diving in a freshwater aquarium, great for the snorkelers of the family.
What age is required for kids?
We do not set a hard age requirement for children. Things to consider include the fact that all customers must wear a full wetsuit. We have child's suits down to a size six. Also, everyone in the water must remain calm and quiet at all times when around manatees. Children must be accompanied by an adult at all times.
How cold is the water?
The water temperature in the spring-fed rivers ranges from 68–74 degrees. Average air temperature ranges from 40–50 degrees at night and 60–70 degrees in the day during the Manatee Season. Our boats are enclosed for comfortable sightseeing!
How close are you to the manatee?
If the manatees were any closer, they would need room keys. Manatee tours take place in Kings Bay (600 acres with a two-mile diameter). Kings Bay is home to the largest concentration of manatees in the world. This is the underwater interactive experience of a lifetime in Crystal River!
Are we safe swimming with the manatees?
Manatees are curious and playful when you are quiet and let them initiate interaction. We show a "manatee manners for swimmers" video before you dive, review a final manatee briefing, and get into the water to videotape and supervise your tour to ensure the best opportunity and manatee encounter for all. Manatees are sensitive to movement and sound, so we do not allow diving into the water, as the bubbles will scare them away. You cannot get underneath these surface dwellers, as it frightens them.On tour, we are in an average of 10 feet of water, and it is against the law to pursue the manatees in any way. So if they are sleeping or eating on the bottom, they should be left alone. It is not difficult to snorkel and most people become comfortable with this diving method. We recommend you practice in our on-site pool if you have an opportunity. This will allow you to be more comfortable in the water. Free manatee literature is available upon request.
Is there a fee for parking?
Because we are leaving from our own private facilities, there is no parking fee like some of our other competitors.
Do you go to Three Sisters on your tours?
Under normal circumstances, we go to Three Sisters on our tours. However, there are days that, depending on weather and tidal conditions, we may use other locations on Kings Bay.

Our Privacy Policy
How We Collect and Treat Your Information
We collect information from you when you register on our site, fill out a form, or make a reservation. When making a reservation or registering on our site, as appropriate, you may be asked to enter your name, e-mail address, mailing address, phone number, or credit card information.
What do we use your information for?

To process transactions
Your information, whether public or private, will not be sold, exchanged, transferred, or given to any other company for any reason whatsoever, without your consent, other than for the express purpose of delivering the purchased product or service requested.
How do we protect your information?
We offer the use of a secure server. All supplied sensitive/credit information is transmitted via Secure Socket Layer (SSL) technology and then encrypted into our database to be only accessed by those authorized with special access rights to our systems and are required to keep the information confidential.
After a transaction, your private information (credit card numbers, social security numbers, financials, etc.) will not be stored on our servers.
Do we use cookies?
Yes. Cookies are small files that a site or its service provider transfers to your computer’s hard drive through your Web browser (if you allow) that enables the sites or service provider’s systems to recognize your browser and capture and remember certain information.
We use cookies to understand and save your preferences for future visits and compile aggregate data about site traffic and site interaction so that we can offer better site experiences and tools in the future. We may contract with third-party service providers to assist us in better understanding our site visitors. These service providers are not permitted to use the information collected on our behalf except to help us conduct and improve our business.
If you prefer, you can choose to have your computer warn you each time a cookie is being sent, or you can choose to turn off all cookies via your browser settings. Like most websites, if you turn your cookies off, some of our services may not function properly. However, you can still place orders over the telephone.
Do we disclose any information to outside parties?
We do not sell, trade, or otherwise transfer to outside parties your personally identifiable information. This does not include trusted third parties who assist us in operating our website, conducting our business, or servicing you, so long as those parties agree to keep this information confidential. We may also release your information when we believe release is appropriate to comply with the law, enforce our site policies, or protect ours or others rights, property, or safety. However, non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing, advertising, or other uses.
Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act Compliance
We are in compliance with the requirements of COPPA (Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act), we do not collect any information from anyone under 13 years of age. Our website, products, and services are all directed to people who are at least 13 years old or older.
Online Privacy Policy Only
This online privacy policy applies only to information collected through our website and not to information collected offline.
Your Consent
By using our site, you consent to our privacy policy.
Changes to our Privacy Policy
If we decide to change our privacy policy, we will post those changes on this page.

Crystal River
Scalloping in
Guests have the opportunity to explore the nearby Gulf of Mexico and discover an abundance of scallops. To embark on a scalloping adventure, one can float along the surface or gently swim over the vast grass flats in water that ranges from four to six feet deep. Once a scallop is spotted, take a deep breath, dive down, and carefully place either your hand or a small dip net under the scallop before gently placing it in your mesh bag. This is an exciting and rewarding experience that allows guests to immerse themselves in the beauty of the Gulf and collect delicious seafood.

TITLE: Alaska Kenai Adventures Lodge | Soldotna, Alaska | ALASKA.ORG
907-252-0705
This family-owned fishing lodge on the Kenai River in Soldotna offers all-inclusive fishing retreats in a stunning location, with private riverbank access and expert guides. The lodge creates one-of-a-kind, unforgettable experiences for guests, families, and groups.
What's Included
Cozy, upscale accommodations with all the modern comforts. Relax in the sauna, gather around the fire pit, or enjoy indoor and outdoor game activities after a day of adventure.
: Enjoy grab and go breakfasts, packed lunches, and chef-prepared dinners.
From rods and reels to high-quality waders, everything is provided.
With local knowledge and years of experience, the guides take you straight to the best fishing spots, maximizing your chances of success.
Cast a line just outside your door.
With two commercial vacuum packers and a flash freezer, the lodge preserves your hard-earned catch so you can enjoy it at home.
Comfortable Basecamp in the Heart of the Kenai Peninsula
The lodge features beautiful cabins that blend rustic charm with modern comforts. You’ll find 18 cabins and never more than 28 guests. Each unit features heating, Starlink Wi-Fi, a private bathroom, and either 2 or 4 beds with hotel-quality bedding; 4 cabins also have kitchenettes. And the lodge is full of amenities. After an adventure-filled day, you can relax in the sauna, gather around the outdoor fire pits, or play horseshoes, corn hole, cribbage, and card games.
Even if you don’t want to fish, the lodge is a great basecamp for hiking or exploring in this gorgeous area.
World-Class Fishing
Whether you’re chasing legendary coho salmon, record-breaking sockeye salmon, mighty halibut, or trout, Alaska Kenai Adventures offers an unparalleled fishing experience.
In the heart of summer, amazing angling is just outside your door. Fish for salmon right from the riverbank; guests may catch their limit in just a few hours and have the rest of the day to go hiking, sightseeing, or golfing at the 9-hole course nearby.
You can also go out with a guide for a charter adventure. One option: Head to another private area just up the river, where you can fish for sockeye salmon that congregate just 10-15 feet off the bank. They’re so abundant that catching your limit is a cinch! Or try your hand at catch-and-release fly fishing for 10 pound-plus rainbow trout—true trophies—in the Kenai River.
You could sample a halibut fishing trip from Homer, Ninilchik or Seward, or go cruising for a day to see glaciers and wildlife in Kenai Fjords National Park from Seward. You’ll also have the option to add on a flyout fishing trip with Talon Air and experience fishing that’s even more remote, along with unforgettable bear-viewing.
Delicious Meals with Fresh Ingredients
Amazing meals are included in your stay and are prepared with fresh ingredients. Some come right from the lodge’s greenhouse, where they grow strawberries, herbs, lettuce and onions.
Start your day off with a grab-and-go-breakfast and get an early start casting on the river. Filling lunches include a take-away box to help propel you through a full day of adventures. And each night you’ll sit down to gourmet dinners in the lodge’s dining room. Don’t miss the locally made beer and wine, available for purchase, from places like Kenai River Brewery and Bear Creek Winery in Homer.
Take Customized Excursions
Beyond fishing, you can customize your all-inclusive stay with a variety of guided excursions that let you explore the breathtaking landscapes and wildlife. Alaska Kenai Adventures will help plan an adventure that fits your Alaskan bucket list.
Examples include:
Cruise past towering glaciers, spot whales, sea lions, and puffins, and witness massive ice calving into the ocean.
Paddle through serene waters surrounded by mountain backdrops and the possibility of spotting bald eagles and harbor seals.
Take to the skies for a once-in-a-lifetime aerial view of Alaska’s vast wilderness, glaciers, and remote wildlife. Land in bear country for a guided viewing experience of these incredible creatures in their natural habitat.
Who Visits the Lodge
Whether you're planning a getaway with friends, a family vacation, or a corporate retreat, the lodge offers the perfect opportunity. Everyone can enjoy the thrill of world-class fishing amid untouched landscapes.
Groups of friends can reel in a trophy salmon and swap stories by the fire. For families, kids will delight in spotting wildlife and catching their first fish, while parents soak in the peaceful beauty of Alaska. And companies looking for a unique retreat can give their employees the chance to step away from the daily grind and bond in a gorgeous setting.

=== PAGE: https://www.alaska.org/detail/between-beaches-cabin-rentals
TITLE: Between Beaches Alaska | Near Homer & Seldovia, Alaska | ALASKA.ORG
907-290-6785
If you can’t decide whether you’d rather have sunset or sunrise views on vacation, this cabin experience is perfect. Perched on a spit near Seldovia that offers both East and West water views, this idyllic spot also offers the chance to watch whales, otters, seals, shorebirds and eagles while enjoying the tranquility of a unique setting.
One Spit, Two Beaches
Located on MacDonald Spit, Between Beaches Alaska is in one sense, self-explanatory.
On one side of the property’s lodging accommodations including six luxury cabins and Beach House, is a beach facing Kachemak Bay, while the other side faces Kasitsna Bay. The beaches are literally a few steps away from each other. It doesn’t matter which side of the spit your cabin is on, you’re welcome to venture to either beach and enjoy private seating and campfire areas. If it’s windy on one beach, it will be calm on the other. On each side you’ll view stunning scenery with majestic snow-capped mountains rising in the distance and abundant wildlife.
Most guests get here by taking the short, scenic water taxi ride from Homer. The water taxi can pull right up to the beach near the cabins and you can easily walk your luggage inside. Some folks, though, take a flight to Seldovia from Homer or Anchorage. From Seldovia a complimentary shuttle service will transport you to MacDonald Spit and the doorstep of your cabin.
Luxury Cabins with Stories
The property is comprised of six cabins; each specifically nestled so that no trees had to be cut down to accommodate their location.
Each cabin has its own personality. , facing Kasitsna Bay, is a cedar cabin that was built in 1955. and , facing Kachemak Bay, were recently handcrafted using reclaimed wood, doors, windows and details from a 1914 cannery in Kenai. These three cabins sleep 3 comfortably including one full and a single size bed. is smaller, perfect for 2. And the is the largest and can sleep 4.
The largest on site is . This stunning cabin is located just 200 feet down the beach from the main property. Enjoy a vaulted ceiling, cozy fireplace, open living area, and 360 degree views of the ocean with private fire pits on each beach. The Beach House sleeps up to 8 with 2 bedrooms and a sleeping loft.
All the cabins feature Kristi’s artwork which include handmade lighting fixtures and unique showers that look like a kelp forest accented with copper and ceramic pieces.
You’ll also find a fully equipped kitchenette: a small 2-burner stove, mini fridge, coffeemaker, and electric tea kettle as well as pots and pans, dishes, utensils, silverware as and cups and glasses. Even pantry essentials like spices, olive oil, paper products, and the all-important coffee are included. Bathrooms come with towels, soap, and shampoos. You will only need to bring groceries, drinks, and personal gear for your stay at Between Beaches Alaska.
Complimentary Equipment and Amenities
Complimentary use of the hot tub and sauna, Kayaks, rowboat, life jackets, paddles and oars are included with the price of all luxury cabins. Each accommodation features private beach seating areas with Adirondak chairs. Buckets, rakes and a boiling pot for harvesting yummy, plentiful mussels and clams and firewood are also provided for your use and pleasure.
Your Host
Your life-long Alaskan host, Kristi, has been spending time on the property since 1968. A commercial fishing career has taken her all over Alaska’s waters, but her favorite fishery is the salmon set-nets right off MacDonald Spit and long-lining halibut.
Visit in Winter
Between Beaches makes the perfect winter getaway too! Enjoy quiet walks along the beach with a campfire on the beach, or gaze up at the stars from the hot tub. Also, a short water taxi ride away is one of the area’s best winter adventures, skating around giant icebergs on Grewingk Glacier Lake, next to the 13-mile-long ice-blue glacier. Pack a picnic lunch and a hot toddy, hop on the water taxi, then take the hour-long hike to the lake, where you can skate around giant icebergs and in the shadow of the gorgeous glacier. Not a skater? You can also explore the icebergs and glacier caves on foot; whichever you do, you’ll get some amazing photos.

=== PAGE: https://www.alaska.org/detail/squid-acres-kennel-dog-sledding-tours
TITLE: Squid Acres Kennel Dog Sledding Tours | Cantwell, Alaska | ALASKA.ORG
907-699-4939
Private Tours in the summer and winter about a 30-minute drive south of Denali National Park
Experience the thrill of the iconic Alaskan sport of dogsledding from veterans of the Iditarod and Yukon Quest races! Operating in summer and winter from Cantwell, about a 30-minute drive south of Denali National Park, the private tours will be just you and your group, led by expert guides.
Winter tours can involve learning to drive your own dog team or riding out to see the northern lights. In summer, the excited dogs pull a side-by-side on wheels across the tundra with a view of Denali. Owners Cody and Paige run the expeditions, along with their team of experienced mushers. And Denali’s a great place to try this amazing sport—not only is it stunning wilderness, but it’s a cooler part of the state to train dogs. So while many summer dogsledding adventures happen on glaciers, you can sample it without the expense of flying to a glacier.
You’ll hear the mushers’ stories and have plenty of opportunities to ask questions. And there will be plenty of time to hang out with the dogs and see them in their “normal” lives cuddling on the couch, but also when they’re doing what they love to do best—running along a trail!
And if you need a place to stay near Denali, Squid Acres has 2 cabins on site that can be booked through Airbnb. These are authentically Alaskan dry cabins, with power but no running water. There’s an outhouse and outdoor sink; inside, each has a queen bed, microwave, refrigerator.
Summer Mushing Experience
Only one private group goes out at a time—anywhere from 2 to 30 people—so you can customize it to focus on what you really want to do. You’ll start off with an hour-long presentation, including the sled, gear, and specialized clothing used when it’s 60-below. You’ll meet the dogs, learn how to harness them up, and hear about the racing process. Then ride along in a side-by-side on a 2-mile route along the Jack River, with a view of Denali on a clear day. Come back and spend some time with the dogs and their puppies!
Winter Mushing Experience
Don layers of warm clothing as you get ready to take on the Alaskan winter wilderness. Learn about the sport while you’re speeding across the snow with your expert guide. Cozy up in warm sleeping bags as you go, or take a turn driving the dogs yourself.
